articles.title_zh: China’s top diplomat calls for expanding cooperation in meeting with South Korean minister
articles.content_orig:
BEIJING, Nov 13 (Reuters) – China is willing to expand cooperation with South Korea in traditional and emerging sectors including ​artificial intelligence and biomedicine, Foreign Minister ‌Wang Yi said on Friday.
• In a meeting with his South Korean counterpart Cho Hyun, Wang said the two countries are “close neighbours that cannot be ‌moved ​away” and “maintaining good-neighbourliness and ⁠friendship is the right ⁠choice for both sides,” according to a statement released by China’s Foreign Ministry
• The South Korean diplomat is on a ​two-day visit to China starting Friday
• China-South Korea relations were “back onto the right ⁠track” after their leaders’ ⁠exchanges since late last year, Wang ​said
• Ties soured under Yoon Suk Yeol, the ​predecessor of South Korean President Lee ‌Jae Myung, who drew Seoul closer to Washington and Tokyo
• Lee, who took office in June 2025, has sought to restore ⁠relations, hosting Chinese President Xi Jinping in Gyeongju in late 2025 and making a state visit to ⁠China in ‌January
• China is willing to ⁠further enhance mutual trust with ​South ‌Korea and expand their common interests, ​Wang said
• ⁠Next week, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung will visit China and attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders’ meeting in Shenzhen
(Reporting by Shi Bu and Ryan Woo; Editing by ​Xevi Fontdegloria)

articles.title_orig: Nasdaq falls on Friday as Nvidia keeps sliding, but major averages are up for week: Live updates
articles.title_zh: Nasdaq falls on Friday as Nvidia keeps sliding, but major averages are up for week: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
Jensen Huang is not the first CEO to leave a company he helped build.
But experts told CNBC that his sudden resignation f rom Nvidia at a critical juncture is unique and leaves his eventual successor with challenges in leading the company that's powering the artificial intelligence boom.
In 33 years, Huang, who resigned on Thursday amid reports of extramarital affairs, including with a woman U.S. intelligence believes is a spy for China , made the company he co-founded the world's most valuable.
Former Goldman Sachs CEO Lloyd Blankfein wrote on X that he was "indispensable" but "the graveyards are filled with indispensable men," referencing a quote attributed to French leader Charles de Gaulle.
While the board looks for a new CEO and CFO Colette Kress does the job temporarily; analysts say Huang's charisma and bullish drive will be hard to replicate.
"I'm not sure we've seen a situation quite like this, where the founder and CEO of one of the world's largest companies faces such a sudden departure amid scandal," Michael Withers, professor of management at the University of Notre Dame's Mendoza College of Business, told CNBC.
Whoever follows will "face challenges that go well beyond those of a typical CEO replacing a founder," he added.
Apple 's image was inseparable from Steve Jobs when he resigned in 2011. But unlike Nvidia, the company had had other CEOs — and an internal successor.
Tim Cook invested in Apple's chip strategy and services business and became a key corporate diplomat in dealings with the U.S. and Chinese governments. He was known as an operator who controlled Apple's supply chain.
Cook had "considerable preparation" for becoming CEO, Withers said. Apple's market cap went from about $350 billion to $4 trillion in his 15-year tenure.
Larry Page and Sergey Brin left their executive roles at Alphabet in 2019, 21 years after founding Google.
Page and Brin's departures were expected. Page said at the time that it was the "natural time" to simplify the company's management structure. Alphabet shares are up more than 300% since then under Sunder Pichai.
Travis Kalanick left Uber in 2017 after mounting pressure over a series of scandals and governance concerns.
But his departure "unfolded over several months, and while it certainly attracted attention, it pales in comparison to what Nvidia is currently facing," Withers added.
Former Expedia CEO Dara Khosrowshahi repaired the organization and found a path to profitability .
Withers said successor CEOs often struggle "under normal circumstances" to juggle maintaining what made a company successful while establishing their own leadership.
"It becomes considerably more difficult when the transition follows such a high-profile scandal involving the company's founder," he added.
Huang had an extraordinary 60 direct reports, as part of a flat structure that favored fast communication over layered hierarchies.
Withers told CNBC Nvidia did not appear to have a succession plan for Huang, who is also often described as inextricably linked to the company.
"We're talking about a company that was, until recently, the largest in the world by market capitalization. That's a pretty remarkable situation," he added.
As well as having to "step out of his shadow," the new CEO will have to deal with the "scandal" arising from Huang's conduct and "the extent to which it sticks with Nvidia," Withers said.
Huang's successor will also have to tackle the longer-term business strategy,  while picking up the relationships he managed.
Huang cultivated a close relationship with U.S. President Donald Trump and accompanied him to China in May . Huang consistently pushed for the U.S. to relax export restrictions that prevent Nvidia from selling its chips to the world's second-largest economy.
He also managed close relationships with the bosses of the company's key suppliers, from SK Hynix to Samsung.
Storm Uru, co-head of the Global Innovation team at Nvidia investor Liontrust Asset Management, said two key priorities were changing company culture and managing the supply chain.
The supply chain was "where Jensen was able to provide a vision for the future and able to bring people to the table and to expand capacity to enable the build-out of this technology," Uru told CNBC, adding it mattered especially "when supply chains are already so tight."
Nvidia continues to face rising competition from rivals such as AMD and hyperscalers, which are ramping up efforts to develop their own chips.
Investors noted that the new CEO will have a roadmap of products for the next few years, unaffected by Huang's removal.
"We have to look beyond Jensen ... there are thousands upon thousands of engineers," Joanne Feeney, partner and portfolio manager, Advisors Capital Management, told CNBC on Thursday, as pressure was mounting on Huang to go.

articles.title_orig: China warns against new U.S. export controls on chips in wake of Nvidia's Huang scandal
articles.title_zh: China warns against new U.S. export controls on chips in wake of Nvidia's Huang scandal
articles.content_orig:
China warned the United States on Friday against imposing additional controls on exports of semiconductors in the wake of the scandal surrounding AI chip giant Nvidia and its now-former CEO Jensen Huang.
China "has consistently opposed the abuse of export control measures, which disrupts the stability of global industrial and supply chains and serves no party's interests," foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told a regular press briefing when asked about calls from U.S. lawmakers to impose more limits on exports of chip equipment to China.
"China and the United States should work together to implement the important consensus reached by their respective heads of state and maintain the stable development of China-U.S. economic and trade relations," Mao said.
Jensen Huang — who resigned Thursday — has admitted to an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. They're not related.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is under fire from critics asking whether his ties to Chinese companies and friendship with Jensen Huang contributed to a lack of oversight by the federal agency over billions in Nvidia AI chip sales, CBS News has learned . The Commerce Department did not respond to a request for comment.
During an interview on CNBC on Friday morning, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent placed the blame on Lutnick's Commerce Department for not including Megaspeed on what's known as the Entity List, which would restrict their ability to access U.S. technology products.
Bessent said that his department, the Defense Department, the State Department and the U.S. trade representative all supported adding Megaspeed to the list.
"They were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the Entity List for months," Bessent said, before referring to the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security. "Commerce BIS has the pen, and you will have to ask them about their internal processes."
According to a U.S. official, Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10.
Last month, the New York Times reported that about a year ago, President Trump was briefed on intelligence that suggested that Alice Huang was a Chinese asset and that she had grown close to Jensen Huang and the president decided not to do anything with the information.
House Speaker Mike Johnson said there's a growing consensus in Congress on further tightening controls on chip exports to China.
According to the Times , U.S. officials circulated a memo last spring citing intelligence alleging that Alice Huang was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, its main intelligence service.
Beijing has rejected the allegations and said on Thursday that they are a "pretext for imposing a technological blockade" to stop China advancing in artificial intelligence technology .

articles.title_orig: Bessent blames Lutnick’s Commerce Department for not restricting Nvidia chips to China
articles.title_zh: Bessent blames Lutnick’s Commerce Department for not restricting Nvidia chips to China
articles.content_orig:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Friday said his department and others in the Trump administration have long supported imposing restrictions on Megaspeed, the company at the center of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 's spy-sex scandal .
But the Commerce Department is in charge "and you will have to ask them about their internal processes," Bessent told CNBC's " Squawk Box ."
The Cabinet secretary's comments hinting at disunity within the administration followed an Axios report that Bessent, in the White House Situation Room last week, had asked Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick why he has resisted implementing export controls, especially on Megaspeed.
Lutnick has "repeatedly stood in the way" of cracking down on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China, Axios reported.
Commerce Department spokeswoman Kristen Eichamer on Wednesday told CNBC that Bessent and Lutnick had "no such conversation" in the Situation Room.
Asked on CNBC about the reported incident, Bessent said, "We don't repeat conversations in the Situation Room."
But he said that the departments of Treasury, Defense and State and the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative all "were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months."
Asked if he was frustrated with the potential export control delays, Bessent said, "I am frustrated when President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s."
"And so any leakage is very frustrating" because it "hurts our great companies in the AI race [and] gives the Chinese an advantage," he said.
Huang, seen as one of Trump's closest corporate allies, resigned as Nvidia CEO on Thursday after admitting to an affair following scrutiny of his relationship with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive whom U.S. intelligence reportedly determined to be a Chinese spy.
Huang had pushed the U.S. government to ease restrictions on the export of advanced AI chips to China. In December, Trump said Nvidia could sell its powerful H200 chips to approved Chinese customers, provided the U.S. gets a percentage of the sales.
Asked if he believes Nvidia's highest-level processors have made it to China using the Singapore-based Megaspeed as a pass-through, Bessent said, "I think that there is a lot of leakage in the system, and we are constantly working to close that down."
"The story has been thus far on Jensen Huang's personal foibles," Bessent told CNBC. "The real story here should be: Did Nvidia know their client, and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?"
"I think it's important that anyone at the company there be held accountable for that," he said.
Huang and Lutnick both have been asked to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month, Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., said Thursday . Huang has separately been asked to sit for a closed-door briefing before multiple House committees on Dec. 1.
The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment on Bessent's remarks.

articles.title_orig: Before he was Pope Leo, he was their bishop. Now he’s back home.
articles.title_zh: Before he was Pope Leo, he was their bishop. Now he’s back home.
articles.content_orig:
By Deborah Castellano Lubov
"Perhaps some of you may think that you have made too many mistakes or that it is already too late to begin again. I would like to say to you: Look to Jesus. He knows your story and continues to invite you to walk with Him."
Pope Leo XIV offered this comforting and concrete reminder during a prayer vigil with young people and university students gathered Thursday evening at the Estadio Nacional in Lima, the final event of his first full day in Peru.
He told them, "You do not need to have your entire future figured out before responding to Him. Take the step you can take today. Trust in His love and allow Him to accompany you. Often, the Lord shows us the way as we walk along it."
In his remarks, the Pope reflected on what young people hope to find in life, acknowledging that some questions can remain with us for a long time.
"Jesus," the Pope reminded them, "is interested in all of this because He is interested in you."
"Do not be afraid to speak to Him sincerely, even when you struggle to find the words to pray," the Holy Father said, noting that "He knows our tears and the questions to which we still have no answers."
He told them that faith sustains us along this path and reminds us that suffering never has the final word. He also encouraged them not to hesitate to seek the company of those who love them, explaining that some sorrows need time and a helping hand.
The Pope urged the young people not to settle for living according to what others expect of them.
"God created you capable of doing a good that no one else can accomplish in exactly the same way."
He acknowledged that, at times, we wonder whether following God's will means giving up our dreams. This fear, he said, can give rise to an even more dangerous suspicion: thinking that God is depriving us of something and that, in order to enjoy life fully, we also need to experience sin (cf. Gen 3:5).
In this context, he said he wished to engrave in their hearts the words of Benedict XVI: "Evil always poisons."
"Do not be deceived! How could something that harms us bring us happiness? God knows our deepest desires even better than we do. He has placed within us the desire to love and to be happy, and He wants to bring that desire to its fullness."
The key to discerning these moments and temptations properly, the Pope said, is learning to recognize the Lord's voice.
"For this reason, dear young people, set aside moments of silence, moments of silence before the Blessed Sacrament, to encounter Him. Speak to Him about your plans and allow His Word to challenge you. Do not be afraid to ask Him what He expects of you. Some of you will be called to the priesthood or consecrated life; others will be called to marriage and to building a family. All of you are called to put your abilities at the service of others."
He stressed that, no matter what we may have done, the Lord continues to knock at the doors of our hearts, inviting us to welcome Him and abide in Him.
"Our vocation, too, grows when we learn to remain close to the Lord, to listen to Him and to share our joys and concerns with Him. In time, those disciples would discover the full extent of His love."
The Pope reminded the young people that this "is the Friend who calls you! Nurture this friendship through prayer, the Eucharist and listening to His Word."
"Do not be afraid to speak about Jesus and to show through your lives how much good His friendship does for you."
He told the Peruvian youth to listen to Jesus' invitation and "dare to follow Him."
The Pope again quoted Benedict XVI, recalling words from a 2005 homily in which he stressed that the Lord "takes nothing away, and He gives you everything."
With this sentiment, Pope Leo urged them to "trust in Christ! Trust in Him as you would in a true friend, one who knows you, loves you and never abandons you."
Finally, the Holy Father concluded by asking the faithful to pray: "Let us ask the Lord, through the intercession of the Virgin Mary and the saints of Peru, to increase this trust each day, to help us live our vocation with passion and to remain always in His friendship."
The Pope concluded by offering the young people "a simple prayer" to help them trust Jesus more and more each day:
Come quickly into my life!

articles.title_orig: Looking Past Nvidia Turmoil, Stocks Set for Best Week in Months
articles.title_zh: Looking Past Nvidia Turmoil, Stocks Set for Best Week in Months
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia was once the stock market’s workhorse. These days, it’s a weakness.
In a stunning turn of events, CEO Jensen Huang, perhaps the AI boom’s most visible cheerleader, resigned Thursday after revelations about a pair of extramarital affairs. Nvidia NVDA stock, which had already struggled in 2026, has lost 14% in the past week and is down roughly 11% for the year.
Meanwhile, thanks to years of huge returns, Nvidia has become one of the most widely held stocks in the market. The Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF (the world’s largest stock fund) has a more than 7% weight in Nvidia, and State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust SPY holds over 6%.
Not only does Huang’s departure from Nvidia create considerable uncertainty about the outlook for the company as a central player in the AI buildout, but it also adds a fresh unknown to a stock market already grappling with a potential data center slowdown in the wake of the Democratic Party’s sweep in the US midterm elections, rising borrowing costs for AI companies, and the impending Anthropic IPO, which is seen as a key test of the market’s appetite for AI stocks.
Nvidia has been the poster child for the AI boom since May 2023, when it reported record quarterly data center sales and issued revenue guidance 50% above the consensus. Those results stunned Wall Street and showed investors that Nvidia had a large AI opportunity. But even then, few grasped the future size of the data center market.
OpenAI’s ChatGPT became a viral sensation upon its release in late 2022, casting a spotlight on generative AI and setting off a global AI arms race. Tech giants Microsoft MSFT , Alphabet GOOG / GOOGL , Amazon AMZN , and Meta Platforms META —now known as hyperscalers, on account of their massive capital expenditures—began buying huge quantities of Nvidia’s chips to train and run AI models. The hyperscalers’ capital expenditures, much of which are spent on chips and other AI-enabling equipment, ballooned from $150 billion in 2023 to an estimated $900 billion this year.
Their spending fueled Nvidia’s explosive growth. Nvidia’s revenue increased $60 million, or 0.2%, in the fiscal year ended January 2023. The next year, sales increased 126%, and they doubled the following year. Nvidia’s revenue is expected to top $409 billion in its current fiscal year, a 1,400% increase in four years.
As Nvidia’s earnings repeatedly blew Wall Street estimates out of the water, investors bid up the company’s stock, fueling a relentless rally. Shares tripled in value in 2023, then more than doubled in 2024.
Nvidia shares more than tripled in value in 2023, when it became only the fifth US company worth more than $1 trillion. The stock more than doubled in value in 2024, when Nvidia became the world’s most valuable company with a market capitalization of more than $3 trillion. It went on to become the world’s first $4 trillion company in July 2025, and topped $5 trillion that October.
Despite the stock’s poor performance this year, Nvidia shares were still up about 1,100% since the end of 2022 at Wednesday’s close, compared with the Morningstar US Total Market Index’s 106% return.
Nvidia’s gains fueled the stock market’s ascent for much of the past four years. Between its first blowout earnings report of the AI boom in May 2023 and the end of 2025, Nvidia alone contributed more than 9 percentage points to the US Total Market Index’s 69% return. Nvidia accounted for more than 13% of the index, which comprises nearly 3,500 stocks. The next-largest contributor, Apple AAPL , added fewer than 4 percentage points.
Nvidia accounted for an even larger share of the gains of smaller indexes. It contributed more than 10 percentage points to the Morningstar US Large Cap Index’s 73% return between May 2023 and the end of 2025.
This year has been a very different story. Shares tread water throughout the first quarter before riding a wave of AI exuberance to a record high in May. They effectively traded sideways until notching a fresh record in early October. Then, mounting concerns about the return on hyperscalers’ AI investments took the wind out of the sails. At Wednesday’s close, shares were 27% off their October highs.
Nvidia has flipped from stock market buoy to burden. It’s been a larger drag on the market than any other stock this year, subtracting 0.4 percentage points from the Total Market Index’s return.
Despite uncertainty about Nvidia’s future leadership, investors bought the dip on Thursday. Shares tumbled as much as 14% in pre-market trading, but closed just 4% lower.
“Deception may have occurred at the CEO level, but it hasn’t crept into Nvidia’s financial forecasts amid the artificial intelligence boom,” says Morningstar senior equity analyst Brian Colello. “We still forecast high near-term and medium-term demand for Nvidia’s gear, given insatiable AI computing growth.”

articles.title_orig: Microsoft 365 Outage Improves Into Friday—Governments, Airlines Report Disruptions
articles.title_zh: Microsoft 365 Outage Improves Into Friday—Governments, Airlines Report Disruptions
articles.content_orig:
A global outage taking down a wide range of Microsoft 365 services remains ongoing Friday morning.
The outage started midday Thursday, impacting users of Microsoft email, cloud, and AI services. Microsoft has documented the full list of services impacted by the error, while moving early Friday morning to protect customers around the world from losing emails during the extended disruptions.
“Recovery actions are ongoing,” the Microsoft 365 Status account confirmed on X. “To help preserve delayed mail during this event, we’ve extended email timeout to 48 hours.”
Similar to recent world-shaking outages of widely used tech like Amazon Web Services and CrowdStrike , the Microsoft disruption looks like “one of the biggest outages of all time,” Ciaran Martin, the former head of the UK’s National Cyber Security Centre, told NBC News . Possibly even “worse,” he suggested.
Businesses, hospitals, police departments, and schools were among those scrambling to work around the outage. In Japan, it disrupted government IT infrastructure, according to deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki. NBC’s report documented various harms, noting that “few public bodies were immune from the outage.” In some cases, doctors couldn’t send patients “important” updates on medication changes or follow-up care.
The financial sector suffered, too, with people blocked from making bank transfers since they couldn’t receive verification codes.
Justice systems were also hobbled. The Supreme Court in the Philippines saw its legal work derailed, NBC reported. And one US sheriff’s office in Colorado reported that the outage made it difficult for people to post bond for prisoners’ immediate release.
It’s unclear how many users were affected, but Microsoft estimated in January that the total number of paid Microsoft 365 commercial subscriptions exceeded 450 million.
On a status page, Microsoft said “we have no evidence of malicious activity associated with this incident” and promised to “share a full Post-Incident Report with root cause and defense-in-depth actions after mitigation is complete.”
“We’re aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact,” Microsoft said on X.
But Microsoft’s public statements make clear that the tech giant was blindsided by the outage and struggled for hours to find mitigations that could reliably restore user access.
Shortly after detecting the outage, Microsoft confirmed that the main issue was “a portion of infrastructure” that “is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions.” This was not caused by increased traffic, Microsoft said, but “a problem that’s causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable.”
Once it became clear that the failed health checks were to blame, Microsoft said it took steps to prevent additional server outages while validating alternate health check methods. But four hours later, the company admitted that it was still in the weeds.
“We’re opening all available pathways to restore service, as our actions taken thus far have not provided the anticipated relief,” Microsoft said. “We found a core process on affected servers is becoming overwhelmed, causing capacity loss. To validate a potential recovery, we’re isolating a portion of infrastructure, restarting affected components, and reintroducing traffic to confirm the services remain stable before applying the change more broadly.”
Even small wins seemed to turn into new setbacks. As Microsoft worked to resolve the issue, some of the servers it brought back online would “become unresponsive again once they receive traffic,” giving the company yet another problem to solve.
Realizing that no quick solutions were coming, Microsoft moved to extend email timeout to 48 hours. As “encouraging” recovery efforts remained ongoing, Microsoft advised users that “some intermittent issues may continue” when traffic is restored.
Microsoft’s most recent updates confirmed that it’s seeing “broader improvements in North America, sustained improvements across much of Europe, and encouraging recovery signals in Asia Pacific.”
“Some users may still experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery as mitigation continues across remaining affected infrastructure,” Microsoft said. “Our focus remains on stabilizing recovered infrastructure, completing mitigation in remaining impacted areas, and reducing delayed email queues and backlogs while we validate service consistency across connection methods.”
DownDetector, which tracks user reports of service issues globally, showed that connectivity losses peaked Thursday afternoon and dropped off substantially by Friday morning.
In comments, an Outlook user described the pains of monitoring email recovery, complaining that outgoing messages seem to send fine but incoming messages are received inconsistently. Some Copilot users seemed distressed that access wasn’t restored as quickly as Outlook. One Microsoft 365 user pondered , “How many offices had people with practically nothing to do? How much has this cost?”

articles.title_orig: Anthropic IPO Share Orders From China Are Said to Be Rebuffed
articles.title_zh: Anthropic IPO Share Orders From China Are Said to Be Rebuffed
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Pershing Square Capital CEO Bill Ackman thinks Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) is a great story with a business that has real potential. Just don't expect him to be a buyer early on when Anthropic becomes publicly traded.
"We think of ourselves as very low-risk investors. We want to invest in businesses that we can predict with a very high degree of confidence," the well-known value investor said at Yahoo Finance Invest. "I think Anthropic is perhaps the most amazing business story of this century in terms of from zero to where it is today — it's an absolutely remarkable story. An incredibly impressive story. I think it's just a much more complicated question as to what that business is worth. It's very hard to nail that with any degree of precision. It could be worth a lot more, a lot less, depending upon a few variables that are difficult to predict. And that's why it doesn't fit into our portfolio."
Anthropic has set an IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share, targeting a fully diluted valuation of approximately $1.4 trillion. The company could raise up to $100 billion from its IPO at the high end of the range.
Read more: Everything you need to know ahead of Anthropic's IPO
But the business has a lot to prove to justify keeping such a lofty valuation in public markets.
In an amended S-1 filing, Anthropic said that third quarter sales rose 1,127% to $17 billion. Revenue growth slowed on a quarter-over-quarter basis. Third quarter sales increased 47% compared with a 144% growth rate in the second quarter. Sales increased 132% in the first quarter.
The company also lost a staggering $23.29 billion in the third quarter.
Anthropic is expected to debut on public markets on Thursday, Nov. 19. It plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.
"I think Anthropic is on the cusp, or might even be at, a place in terms of its operating profitability, where it's real operating profitability," Ackman added. "I think the issue is if Anthropic doesn't stay in the lead position, then the real questions about the business model [emerge]. So the capex they have to spend is really real … So I would just say it's a much more complicated question. And there's a much wider range of outcomes — it's a more speculative bet than buying, for example, Visa, a company we own."

articles.title_zh: NYC Council passes ban on 'surveillance pricing' that relies on personal data

Make your contribution now and help Gothamist thrive in 2026. Donate today

The City Council passed a bill Thursday that bans companies in New York City from using surveillance pricing, which charges different prices based on algorithms or shoppers’ personal data.
Surveillance pricing means shoppers see a price based on their personal data like demographics, credit, browsing history or purchasing history. The bill prohibits surveillance pricing both online and in stores, although the practice is mainly used on the web.
Speaker Julie Menin described surveillance pricing as an “insidious and predatory corporate practice” that erodes privacy and fairness.
“It's a practice that worsens the affordability crisis, and today it's a practice that we are going to be ending,” she said during a press conference ahead of the vote.
In one investigation cited by the Council, Target shoppers saw a jump in pricing based on location data showing whether they were inside or outside a store. Shoppers found that a 55-inch SmartTV cost $499 on the Target app when inside a store, and $599 when in the store parking lot.
Uber, Lyft, Target, Instacart and airlines are among the companies that have faced scrutiny for alleged surveillance pricing. Many of the companies have denied using the practice.
Under the bill, the city would be able to issue fines of up to $1,000 for each transaction that violates the ban.
Menin’s proposal follows legislation approved by Albany lawmakers in June that prohibits surveillance pricing online and in stores, with some exceptions.
Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a statement that he supports the ban. He called surveillance pricing “just another way corporations are finding to squeeze working people.”
“New Yorkers’ personal data should never be used as a weapon against their own pocketbooks,” he added.
Business groups have warned that the ban could hinder discounts or loyalty programs for customers.
“If enacted, this law will make it harder for small restaurants with limited marketing budgets to reach customers, putting them at a disadvantage against national chains,” said Josh Gold, a spokesperson for Uber.
The company operates Uber Eats, which allows restaurants to offer discounts based on search history and previous orders.
Menin said the legislation would not affect discounts.

articles.title_orig: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq futures edge higher after wholesale inflation grows, Nvidia stock rebounds
articles.title_zh: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq futures edge higher after wholesale inflation grows, Nvidia stock rebounds
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
US stocks fell Friday as a sell-off in chip stocks picked up, Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock continued to decline, and an annual reading of wholesale inflation came in hot.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) edged lower by 0.2%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) declined 0.9%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) fell 1.6%.
Stocks sank amid a series of tremors, from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepping down to elevated oil prices and a sell-off in government bonds.
Nvidia stock turned lower again as the fallout from Huang's affairs continued to unfold, raising the stakes for the company's third quarter earnings next Tuesday. Investors are debating whether the controversy surrounding the chip giant's former leader implicates the wider artificial intelligence boom that Nvidia has played a central role in building.
Chipmaker sector stocks declined, with AMD ( AMD ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) sinking.
Oil prices were little changed, providing some relief after a spike in prices sparked Thursday's sell-off in bonds. As traders braced for an interest rate hike in December, the 10-year Treasury yield ( ^TNX ) reached as high as 5.17% on Friday, its highest level since October.
The setup has pressured bitcoin ( BTC ), with the world's largest cryptocurrency tumbling below $70,000 Friday for the first time in nearly three months.
In economic news, wholesale inflation rose 0.3% month over month in October, according to the producer price index. The reading was less than the 0.4% economists expected, but the annual rate of 6.5% highlighted persistent inflation pressures, which likely keeps the Federal Reserve on track to hike interest rates next month.
Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock slipped more than 4% on Friday as a sell-off in the semiconductor sector accelerated and investors digested the exit of Jensen Huang as CEO of the AI chip heavyweight, following reports of multiple affairs. The stock is expected to close out the week in the red, slipping below the $4 trillion market cap threshold.
Shares of chipmaker peers AMD ( AMD ), Broadcom ( AVGO ) and Intel ( INTC ) dropped roughly 9%, 6% and 5%, respectively.
Storage maker Sandisk ( SNDK ) stock extended declines from the prior session, falling 9%. Shares of memory chipmakers Micron Technology ( MU ) and SK Hynix ( SKHY ) also tanked 5% and 6%, respectively.
Wall Street's fear gauge jumped Friday as investors grew more uncertain about the stock market amid broader inflation worries and the Nvidia ( NVDA ) tumult.
The Cboe Volatility Index, or VIX ( ^VIX ), climbed above 20 in morning trading, extending a muted rise on Thursday as the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 were mixed.
The latest jump marks a sharp reversal from earlier this week, when volatility expectations retreated following last week's post-election market turmoil. The VIX surged nearly 70% on Nov. 5, one of its largest daily increases this year.
The index, which tracks expectations for S&P 500 volatility over the next 30 days, has averaged roughly 18.2 in 2026, according to Yahoo Finance data. Its recent swings underscore how quickly investors' appetite for risk has shifted.
Still, stocks are holding on to gains for the week.
Yahoo Finance's Paige Oamek reports:
Richemont stock opened more than 4% lower on Friday morning as the Swiss luxury group reported slower growth in its jewelry business.
The owner of Cartier and Van Cleef & Arpels posted first-half net profit of 2.5 billion euros (approximately $2.76 billion), up from 1.8 billion euros ($2 billion) a year earlier and above analyst forecasts of 2.26 billion euros ($2.5 billion).
But eyes were on jewelry, the group's growth engine, where sales rose 14%, short of the 16% analysts had expected, according to an RBC poll.
Many luxury brands have struggled amid foreign conflicts, rising gold prices, and cost-sensitive consumers. The luxury sector has fallen some 30% in 2026, per Barron's.
Wholesale inflation data came in better than expected for the month of October, but the long-term trend painted a worrying picture of rising prices.
The Producer Price Index, a measure of wholesale inflation, rose 0.3% month over month in October, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on Friday. Economists had expected PPI to increase 0.4%.
However, over the last 12 months, the index for final demand increased 6.5% in October, the largest annual increase since November 2022.
That keeps the pressure on the Fed to raise interest rates next month.
Fed governor Michelle Bowman said Tuesday that rate hikes may be needed to slow the pace of price increases, Yahoo Finance's Jennifer Schonberger reported.
"Inflation pressures have persisted for longer than I had hoped and have shown recent signs of broadening," Bowman said in a speech in Washington.
US stocks opened higher on Friday as investors looked to close out a volatile week marked by rising Treasury yields, renewed pressure from oil prices and turmoil at Nvidia.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) rose 0.4%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) gained 0.4%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) was flat.
Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares rose 2% as investors continued to assess the fallout from Jensen Huang's departure ahead of the chipmaker's earnings next week. Other semiconductor stocks remained under pressure.
Investors were also watching the 10-year Treasury yield, which climbed to 5.10% Thursday.
The bull market won't have it easy in 2027, Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi reports. According to Goldman Sachs strategist Kamakshya Trivedi, the vibes around AI investments are weakening.
Here's what Trivedi had to say about risks to stocks:
"Although we expect solid AI investment growth to continue, our forecasts imply that the investment growth impulse — additional AI investment as a share of GDP — will peak in early 2027. From a macro perspective, this should be a manageable event. But it may be a bigger test for markets for three reasons."
"First, the AI impulse has been a much larger contributor to growth in earnings and market value than to growth in GDP," Trivedi explained.
"Second, AI-related equities have taken credit for significant macro productivity gains, especially companies benefiting directly from the infrastructure boom, that have made them more vulnerable to any signs that we are on a less optimistic path," Trivedi added.
"Third, the point at which growth rates peak (a "second derivative" turning point) often matters, even if underlying growth rates (the "first derivative") remain healthy. Moving through that peak allows markets to place limits on the upside of an uncertain distribution and, as growth decelerates, the period of positive surprises to expectations often ends too, as we may be starting to see for the AI capex cycle."
Cerebras Systems ( CBRS ) stock jumped 13% in premarket trading after the AI chipmaker reported record third quarter revenue and raised its full-year outlook.
The company's core revenue rose 70% year over year to $230.9 million while cloud revenue surged 272% to $144.9 million. The maker of AI chips, looking to compete with Nvidia ( NVDA ), said it sees fourth quarter core revenue of $310 million to $330 million, versus Wall Street consensus estimates of $271.2 million.
The company also announced commercial deals with two new hyperscalers, or large cloud computing providers that operate data centers. One is among the world's top three, with Cerebras saying it would share more details about the deal next year.
"These new deals, alongside continued growth and execution with our existing customers, enable us to raise Q4 core guidance across the board and continue to see revenue tripling in 2027 with expanding gross margins," Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman said during the company's earnings call on Thursday.
The cheapest way for an American company to run AI is a free model made in China. The scandal that just cost Nvidia its CEO could shut off the chips those models depend on, Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre writes.

articles.title_orig: US Wholesale Inflation Picks Up to Fastest Pace Since 2022
articles.title_zh: US Wholesale Inflation Picks Up to Fastest Pace Since 2022
articles.content_orig:
Wholesale prices increased less than expected in October, but inflation pressures persisted and the Federal Reserve is likely still on target for an interest rate increase soon.
The producer price index , which measures the prices domestic producers get for their products before they reach the consumer, rose a seasonally adjusted 0.3% for the month, against the Dow Jones consensus for a 0.4% increase, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Friday.
Stripping out food and energy, core PPI posted a 0.3% gain, meeting expectations.
On an annual basis, headline PPI accelerated 6.5%, up 0.2 percentage point for the highest annual rate since November 2022.
The report comes just a few weeks ahead of the Federal Reserve's next policy meeting, Dec. 8-9. Markets are fully pricing in a quarter percentage point increase in the central bank's key overnight borrowing rate, with slight odds that the Federal Open Market Committee might opt for a half-point hike.
Stock market futures added to gains following the release while Treasury yields were mixed.
Earlier this week, the BLS reported that inflation at the cash register was hotter than expected.
The headline consumer price index saw a 0.4% increase in October while core was up 0.3%, both 0.1 percentage point higher than expected. Because of the government shutdown in October 2025, the BLS couldn't collect some data and refrained from putting out a 12-month inflation figure for CPI.
However, the figures showed that the Fed remains a good distance from its 2% inflation goal.
"Today's PPI data – which shows some signs of improving, albeit still too-high – is unlikely to change the Fed's approach in December because the CPI data was already outside their comfort zone," said Chris Zaccarelli, chief investment officer for Northlight Asset Management.
Moreover, policymakers are beginning to worry that inflation generated by the Iran war and higher fuel prices, along with President Donald Trump's tariffs, are beginning to spread through the economy. The Fed generally would look through such price pressures as temporary, but the breadth of inflation could indicate that inflation is becoming more entrenched.
"We've had some signs of trouble now for several months in a row," Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said in a CNBC interview Friday. "If you look at how broad-based the inflation is, it's not just that we're above the target and have been for some time. It's that in categories that are not driven by oil prices and not driven by tariffs, you're still seeing stalled progress and in some cases going the wrong way."
Stripping out food, energy and trade services, PPI saw an increase of 0.5% in October.
Goods prices increased 0.5% in October, with more than 60% of that move driven by goods excluding food and energy, which actually saw a 0.1% decrease. On an annual basis, the goods index jumped 10.2%, the biggest 12-month surge since October 2022.
Final demand services prices increased 0.2%, most of which was linked to transportation and warehousing services, and within that category a 3.9% gain in truck transportation of freight.
"We've been above 2% for almost six years, and while it sometimes we were making progress, lately we're not making any progress, and if anything, it's going the wrong way," Goolsbee said. "Inflation is rising; it's proved far more persistent than we predicted at the beginning from the supply shocks."
Other items in the PPI report also showed multiyear gains. Prices for intermediate processed goods soared 14.6% from October 2025, the biggest annual gain since July 2022. Intermediate prices for services posted a 6.9% increase, the most since November 2022.

SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 is the 15th test flight of Starship, the world's largest and most powerful rocket. SpaceX has designed the rocket to be fully reusable, and has landed its massive Super Heavy first stage booster several times.
Flight 15 is SpaceX's first attempt to land both the Super Heavy booster and its Ship upper stage by returning them to their launch pad and catching them in the pad's metal "Chopstick" arms. The landings will be about 22 hours apart, with Super Heavy landing minutes after launch and the Ship upper stage returning to Starbase on Saturday afternoon.

articles.title_orig: Europe pushes for a seat at Ukraine peace talks‌ but lacks a unified voice
articles.title_zh: Europe pushes for a seat at Ukraine peace talks‌ but lacks a unified voice
articles.content_orig:
DUBLIN —  EU leaders gathering in Dublin on Friday will continue arguing over who should represent them in talks about Ukraine’s future after a day of ferocious diplomatic activity.
As Donald Trump’s administration intensifies its efforts to broker an end to Russia’s war and Europe may have secured a place at the table, bickering over who will speak on behalf of the bloc already looks like overshadowing the summit in the Irish capital — that wasn’t even supposed to be about Ukraine in the first place.
“You could even have a TV show about it,” Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal joked to POLITICO in an interview on Thursday, in a sign of just how stark the divisions have become among leaders. “But we are saving the best part for tomorrow.”
Russia’s full-scale invasion started in February 2022 and as Trump’s enthusiasm for brokering peace has ebbed and flowed, the EU has found itself edged out of the picture ― despite increasingly picking up the tab .
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who met with about 50 EU and non-EU leaders in Dublin on Thursday, warned that Russia was seeking to reshape Europe’s security architecture and insisted that European governments must have a voice in the negotiations, following two days of Russia-Ukraine-U.S. negotiations in Abu Dhabi that largely left out the EU.
Trump’s envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, discussed the issue with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow earlier on Thursday before the American pair touched down in Dublin in the evening to offer Zelenskyy their thoughts.
The EU is united over the need to have a seat at the table as Ukraine’s main backer, but not on who it should send, with diplomats and officials telling POLITICO that the bloc has split into at least three camps.
In one, there is growing support for European Council President António Costa, whose role makes him the natural candidate to represent the bloc. In another, there’s France and Germany, both of which are reluctant to surrender their own places at the negotiating table to Brussels.
And then there’s the loneliest camp of all, the backers of Kaja Kallas. The bloc’s top diplomat would be the obvious pick, if not for her hawkishness on Russia, which some diplomats say could put off the Kremlin and make her a liability.
When it comes to speaking for Europe, there’s one man who’s already got that in his job description.
Costa is emerging as the most broadly acceptable candidate among EU capitals. His institutional role gives him a mandate to represent the bloc’s leaders on the world stage, while his position and background as a former Portuguese prime minister afford him some neutrality, according to a European diplomat, who was granted anonymity because of the sensitive nature of the discussions.
Estonia’s Michal was the first leader to come out in support of Costa, telling POLITICO his “mandate comes directly from the [European] Council” and makes him “accountable” to the EU’s member countries.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, who called for the issue to be added to the agenda of Friday’s talks, said she would be OK with Costa, while Luxembourg and Poland’s leaders also backed him in remarks to reporters Thursday.
Costa himself has also made it clear that the EU is represented internationally by its institutions — meaning him.
Kallas, however, is a much more divisive proposition.
Some diplomats see the former Estonian prime minister, who an EU official once said eats “Russians for “breakfast,” as an unacceptable interlocutor for the Kremlin.
“That’s a joke, right?” another European diplomat said of the prospect of Kallas representing the EU in the high-stakes talks, describing her as “probably the worst person you could pick.”
But others argue that it’s precisely this hawkish reputation that makes her the right person for the job. “It would make much more sense,” a second senior European diplomat told POLITICO. “That’s what Putin would do. He would pick whoever you don’t want to talk to.”
Michal argued Kallas’ role makes her a natural second to Costa, and that both will presumably be in their positions until their terms end in 2029, making them more reliable than a national leader. “Putin doesn’t have to like it,” he added.
The biggest obstacle to choosing a negotiator, though, might not be Putin but the EU’s two biggest capitals.
France and Germany are unlikely to welcome an arrangement that gives Brussels a monopoly on representing Europe in negotiations, two European diplomats and an EU official told POLITICO.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made his opposition clear Thursday, calling the participation of the E3 countries in talks on Ukraine “a well-established format.”
“We are also working together on this task with five representatives — from Germany, the United Kingdom, France, Italy, and Poland. I see absolutely no problem with keeping it that way,” he said.
Paris also has little incentive to hand over its seat at the table. France is a permanent member of the United Nations Security Council and possesses Europe’s only nuclear arsenal, giving it diplomatic and military leverage that no EU institution can replicate, French MEP Fabrice Leggeri of National Rally told POLITICO, adding he could “hardly imagine” Costa or Kallas speaking for Paris.
“France, Germany, and the U.K.,” the E3 countries, “will always be France, Germany and the U.K.,” Estonia’s Michal argued, adding nothing stopped them from talking bilaterally to Moscow. But on decision-making affecting the whole continent, they needed to get on board with “consensual politics.”
“This is what the European Union is,” he said. “This is the basis of having this kind of consensual politics and keeping everybody together on the same page against Russia.”
EU leaders are unlikely to formally appoint an envoy at Friday’s gathering, but discussions could produce a broader “understanding” about how Europe should be represented, a senior EU official said.
Irish Foreign Minister Helen McEntee told POLITICO that at Friday’s talks, leaders will still need to “tease through” the issue “a little bit more.”
They may not have that much time, though. Zelenskyy this week urged the EU to hurry up and pick someone — anyone — to speak for it. “I think that in November, not later, we need to accept who will represent Europe in negotiations,” he said.
Giorgio Leali, Hans von der Burchard, Jacopo Barigazzi and Caroline Hug contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Commerce Secretary Lutnick agreed to testify on Nvidia's AI chip sales to China
articles.title_zh: Commerce Secretary Lutnick agreed to testify on Nvidia's AI chip sales to China
articles.content_orig:
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee, as the fallout from ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy intensifies.
Lutnick was summoned by Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott amid scrutiny over whether Nvidia could have supplied advanced artificial intelligence chips to Chinese companies and thereby potentially threatened U.S. national security.
Huang and Lutnick both received letters on Thursday evening requesting them to testify in separate hearings on Dec. 3 and Dec. 10, respectively. The letter to Lutnick asked the commerce secretary to testify regarding "recent public reports about NVIDIA and the Department of Commerce's role that raises national security concerns."
"Secretary Lutnick has proactively agreed to appear voluntarily before the Banking Committee to address their questions," Kristen Eichamer, a spokesperson for Lutnick, told NBC News on Thursday. CNBC contacted the Commerce Department for comment.
The letter to Huang said that reports about his relationship with the alleged Chinese spy "raise significant national security concerns."
Huang has acknowledged an affair with an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that has bought over $4.8 billion of advanced Nvidia AI chips over the past two years. The scandal, in addition to reports of a separate affair with a senior executive at Nvidia, led to his resignation on Thursday.
There is growing bipartisan scrutiny of the Commerce Department Secretary's approach to chip policy and whether his department was doing enough to restrict the supply of AI chips to China. Lawmakers are also questioning whether the department was overseeing Nvidia's exports thoroughly enough
Senator Jim Banks has been particularly scathing, saying Lutnick "appears to have used loopholes to allow some of these chip sales to occur," in an appearance on Fox News on Thursday.
Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass, who will chair the Senate Banking Committee from January, said on Thursday "Secretary Howard Lutnick and Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler must explain why they have not closed export control loopholes and act today to ensure our advanced technology is not fueling China's military."
In a joint letter with incoming Senate Foreign Relations Chair Chris Coons published Wednesday, they said all documents relating to the export of Nvidia chips to China must be preserved.
Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore. and Rep. Richard E. Neal, D-Mass. told Lutnick they were investigating the approval of sales of Nvidia chips to companies with links to the Chinese government, military and sanctioned entities.
Rep. Brian Mast, R-Fla. said on Thursday that Congress needed to investigate the role of the Commerce Department in approving the export to China of AI chips, but added that he had confidence in Lutnick.
Criticism is mounting on President Donald Trump 's administration for declining to include over 100 companies highlighted as national security risks on a trade blacklist, including China's AI startup DeepSeek and memory chipmaker CXMT, Reuters reported in June.
Lutnick is a long-standing friend of Trump, with their relationship spanning over three decades, and is widely regarded as a close confidant of the President.

articles.title_orig: The Fed chief said AI would tame inflation. His colleagues disagree.
articles.title_zh: The Fed chief said AI would tame inflation. His colleagues disagree.
articles.content_orig:
Chicago Federal Reserve President Austan Goolsbee expressed concern about the latest inflation data, telling CNBC on Friday that the central bank likely will need to take action.
"I believe that the the central bank has definitely got work to do to continue to reestablish its credibility," the policymaker said during an interview on "Squawk Box."
His remarks came shortly after the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the producer price index , considered a proxy for wholesale prices, posted a 0.3% increase in October, which was slightly less than expected, but also indicated a 6.5% annual gain, the highest since November 2022.
With data in hand earlier in the week showing that the consumer price index rose a bit more than expected during the month, Goolsbee said the Fed is slipping further away from its 2% inflation target.
"We've been above 2% for almost six years, and while it sometimes we were making progress, lately we're not making any progress, and if anything, it's going the wrong way," he said.
"Inflation is rising. It's proved far more persistent than we predicted at the beginning from the supply shocks, and now we're adding this old-fashioned demand overheating coming from the AI data center buildout, that looks like it's starting to spread out of its lane," Goolsbee added.
Markets are fully pricing in a quarter percentage point increase when the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee meets next on Dec. 8-9. There also is a better than 10% probability of a half-point hike, according to the CME Group's FedWatch gauge of futures markets. Goolsbee is not currently an FOMC voter but will be in 2027.
Earlier in the week, Fed Governor Christopher Waller indicated he would entertain a 50 basis point move depending on this week's inflation data.
Goolsbee did not speculate directly on whether the Fed might need to be more aggressive.
"It's it's all going to be about this ... question: What is happening to inflation, and are we on path back to 2%?" he said. "My feeling is, right now we're not."

articles.title_orig: Another Update About The ‘GTA 6 Online’ Release Date
articles.title_zh: Another Update About The ‘GTA 6 Online’ Release Date
articles.content_orig:
Get unlimited access to everything VICE has to offer.
With the Grand Theft Auto VI preload now live, a new PS5 datamine has players wondering when they might get to explore Vice City with friends. So, is GTA 6 going to have online multiplayer, and is there a release date yet? Here’s what dataminers found and what we know so far.
GTA 6 is going to be single-player only at launch on November 19, 2026. Since its announcement, Rockstar has consistently described the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S release as a “single player experience,” and there’s still no official GTA 6 Online release date or window.
In fact, Rockstar has yet to even officially announce an online mode for Grand Theft Auto VI . However, a recent GTA 6 PS5 datamine may have given us our first clue about the much-anticipated multiplayer mode. On November 9, PlayStation Game Size reported finding three entries in the PlayStation database tied to Grand Theft Auto VI :
Grand Theft Auto VI supports : intentType": "joinSession" intentType": "launchActivity" intentType": "launchMultiplayerActivity"
Those entries point to PS5 features that let you jump into an activity or join a session. The multiplayer entry is the one that particularly stands out, since it suggests there could be a way to launch an online activity separately from Jason and Lucia’s story.
Popular Rockstar dataminer TexFunz2 has also suggested that players might be able to install the story and multiplayer separately. That said, at the time of writing, no a GTA 6 online mode has not been confirmed. But datamine files suggest it could get multiplayer support in the future .
As of November 10, 2026, Rockstar Games and Take-Two haven’t announced a GTA 6 Online release date or window. November 19 is when Grand Theft Auto VI launches on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Take-Two’s November earnings release lists that same date for the game and gives no launch timing for a new online mode.
If you’ve seen 2027 mentioned for a GTA 6 online release date, that comes from Twitch CEO Dan Clancy. In a September interview with Bloomberg, Clancy said he’d spoken with Rockstar and expected an even bigger bump in viewership the following year when multiplayer launches. However, 2027 is a window Clancy “expected” and not a date Rockstar has announced or confirmed.
Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked in February what would happen to the current version of GTA Online once GTA 6 came out. He said he had “every reason to believe we’ll continue to support GTA Online,” pointing to the players who still show up when Rockstar adds new content.
Take-Two went a step further at its September shareholder meeting and said support would continue after GTA 6 launches. So if you want to play GTA with friends on November 19, you’ll still be able to jump into the existing GTA Online . For Vice City, November 19 is when you can start Jason and Lucia’s story.

articles.title_orig: Scoop: Israeli spy chief in D.C. as Netanyahu presses Trump to resume war
articles.title_zh: Scoop: Israeli spy chief in D.C. as Netanyahu presses Trump to resume war
articles.content_orig:
Despite losing its majority in last month’s parliamentary elections, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government is still in power in a caretaker capacity.
That will continue until a new governing majority is formed – a process that could take months as Israel’s opposition struggles to form a coalition.
And while he may be politically weakened, Netanyahu is reported to be weighing new military action against Iran , despite a lack of enthusiasm from the United States, his own military establishment, and the politicians vying to replace him.
But does Netanyahu’s caretaker government actually have the authority to send Israel back to war, and how would such a move be received at home?
Officially, Israel’s caretaker government has the same authority as a regular government. Article 30 of the country’s Basic Law states that an interim government continues to carry out the same duties until a new one takes its place.
However, Israel’s Supreme Court has previously ruled that an outgoing government must avoid irreversible policy moves unless they are urgent – a principle known as the “duty of restraint”.
In practice, Netanyahu can still initiate military action with the approval of his caretaker government, which he could present as “urgent and in the national interest”, Neve Gordon, a professor of international law at Queen Mary University, London, and the author of “Israel’s Occupation”, told Al Jazeera.
Or Asher, a researcher at the Tel Aviv-based Tachlith Institute, told the Reuters news agency that security issues generally are “the clearest exception” to a caretaker government’s duty of restraint.
“The Supreme Court has historically avoided intervening in decisions to go to war, and parliamentary oversight is at its thinnest in the weeks after the new Knesset [parliament] ⁠⁠convenes and before its committees are formed,” said Asher.
“A caretaker prime minister can legally take Israel to war, including against Iran,” he added.
Ehab Jabareen, an analyst and Palestinian citizen of Israel, told Al Jazeera the government’s caretaker status raises the “political burden of proof”.
“Netanyahu would be asking the country to accept the consequences of a decision that could outlast his government,” he said.
On Wednesday, Israeli media reported that the security cabinet chaired by Netanyahu had ordered the military to step up preparations for an attack on Iran.
“The directives issued by the security cabinet to the Israeli military could lead it to carry out activities that could trigger a war,” public broadcaster KAN reported.
That followed reports that Netanyahu has been repeatedly calling US President Donald Trump to press for a new military campaign against Iran, conversations that on at least one occasion became heated, according to Israel’s Ynet News site.
On Thursday, a US military official was quoted by KAN as saying that Washington had told Israel to get ready for a potential new round of confrontation. But the US military’s Central Command (CENTCOM) later dismissed the reports, telling Al Jazeera they were “mere speculation”.
According to Israel’s Channel 13, the Israeli military establishment sees no urgent need to attack Iran. It said that assessment had been presented to Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, who has been tasked with forming the next government, during a briefing on Wednesday.
The opposition has demanded that Netanyahu avoid any military action unless it is critical.
Yisrael Beytenu leader Avigdor Lieberman, a member of the opposition bloc, said the prime minister’s caretaker government must not “make decisions that could drag Israel into war without parliamentary oversight and without the full agreement of all security officials”.
Eisenkot echoed this sentiment in a letter to Netanyahu on Wednesday, saying that deploying Israeli forces “without a direct and immediate threat that cannot wait could have devastating consequences for Israeli democracy and public trust in the institutions of government”.
The Israeli premier responded by insisting the government makes all decisions based only on “security considerations”.
There would be serious divisions.
“Obviously, those who voted for Netanyahu and parties from his coalition would be in favour, while most of those who supported the so-called change bloc would be upset at Netanyahu’s use of the war to try to remain in power and block their electoral success,” said Gordon.
But ultimately, he said, most people who voted against Netanyahu’s bloc would “rally around the flag” if he resumes hostilities.
Jabareen agreed that Israelis would likely rally if a new war breaks out and missiles are incoming. But he said that “tells you very little about whether they think Netanyahu was right to start another round [of conflict]”.
“And the harder test comes when reservists are called up again, families are back in shelters and the government has to explain what the campaign can achieve that the previous one didn’t,” he added.
Jabareen said the debate in Israel over any new confrontation on Iran would likely centre on “why now?”
“If the case for urgency is weak, especially if Washington is opposed and senior Israeli commanders have reservations, the decision could be seen as an attempt to change the political agenda while Eisenkot is trying to form a government,” he said.
Beyond domestic considerations, an obstacle to Netanyahu restarting attacks may be the position of Israel’s main ally, the US, which has said it is doubling down on its economic pressure campaign against Iran rather than pursuing more large-scale military action.
“Netanyahu’s problem … is not the Israeli public, but what seems to be a loss of appetite in the US,” said Gordon.
Anders Persson, a political scientist specialising in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, said it would be easier for Netanyahu to pull off a new military campaign if it is undertaken jointly with the US.
But “the more openly Netanyahu provokes Iran, and the less support he receives from Trump, the harder it will be for him to get away with it – and for the Israeli public to accept it”, Persson told Al Jazeera.
Yes. And in one case, the government was led by Netanyahu himself.
In May 2021, weeks after his party lost seats in legislative elections and while negotiations for a new government were under way, the prime minister launched an 11-day war in Gaza that killed at least 260 people in the Palestinian enclave. Thirteen people also died in Israel.
While that conflict temporarily stalled efforts to replace Netanyahu, a new government, led by Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, was formed the following month, ending a 12-year run as prime minister .
Former Israeli prime ministers Ehud Olmert and Yair Lapid also ordered military action in Gaza while serving in a caretaker capacity. The 2008 war directed by Olmert was by far the most deadly , killing about 1,400 Palestinians.

articles.title_orig: Stock Market Today: Nvidia Set to Recoup Some Losses After Huang's Exit — Live Updates
articles.title_zh: Stock Market Today: Nvidia Set to Recoup Some Losses After Huang's Exit — Live Updates
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia shares were slightly higher in premarket trading on Friday as investors navigate the fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation after reports of at least two affairs.
It follows a wild day for the stock on Thursday, which dropped sharply before recovering to close just over 4% lower.
Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia on Thursday after The New York Times reported that Huang had a romantic relationship with Kimberly Powell, vice president of health care at Nvidia.
Huang was already under scrutiny following an investigation by the board into his relationship with a businesswoman who intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy.
Reuters reported on Thursday the existence of another affair with an Nvidia employee, which the news agency did not name. Nvidia did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.
Shares of Nvidia were 1.7% higher as of 8:13 a.m. ET.
Before Huang resigned, several Wall Street analysts told CNBC that his departure could cost Nvidia as much as 20% of its market value, given how critical he has been to the company's success. Nvidia's stock is already down more than 20% over the last month.
A lot of the company's success has been built around Huang, said Stephane Houri, head of equity research at ODDO BHF.
It's about more than just Nvidia, but also about the "architecture of the AI industry that really depended on the vision" and expertise of Huang, Houri told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Friday.

articles.title_zh: Watch CNBC's full interview with Treasury Sec. Scott Bessent on Nvidia, China trade
articles.content_orig:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Friday said his department and others in the Trump administration have long supported slapping restrictions on Megaspeed, the company at the center of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's spy-sex scandal.
But the Commerce Department is in charge, "and you will have to ask them about their internal processes," Bessent told CNBC's "Squawk Box."
The Cabinet secretary's comments hinting at disunity within the administration followed an Axios report that Bessent, in the White House Situation Room last week, had asked Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick why he has resisted implementing export controls, especially on Megaspeed.
Lutnick has "repeatedly stood in the way" of cracking down on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China, Axios reported.
Commerce Department spokeswoman Kristen Eichamer on Wednesday told CNBC that Bessent and Lutnick had "no such conversation" in the Situation Room.
Asked on CNBC about the reported incident, Bessent said, "We don't repeat conversations in the Situation Room."
But he said that the departments of Treasury, Defense and State and the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative all "were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months."
Asked if he was frustrated with the potential export control delays, Bessent said, "I am frustrated when President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s."
"And so any leakage is very frustrating" because it "hurts our great companies in the AI race [and] gives the Chinese an advantage," he said.
Huang, seen as one of Trump's closest corporate ally before resigning as Nvidia CEO under a cloud of scandal Thursday morning, had pushed the U.S. government to ease restrictions on the export of advanced AI chips to China. In December, Trump said Nvidia could sell its powerful H200 chips to approved Chinese customers, provided the U.S. gets a percentage of the sales.
This is breaking news. Please check back for updates.

articles.title_orig: Wholesale prices rose 0.3% in October, putting annual rate at 6.5%, the highest in nearly four years
articles.title_zh: Wholesale prices rose 0.3% in October, putting annual rate at 6.5%, the highest in nearly four years
articles.content_orig:
Wholesale prices increased less than expected in October, but inflation pressures persisted and the Federal Reserve is likely still on target for an interest rate increase soon.
The producer price index , which measures the prices domestic producers get for their products before they reach the consumer, rose a seasonally adjusted 0.3% for the month, against the Dow Jones consensus for a 0.4% increase, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Friday.
Stripping out food and energy, core PPI posted a 0.3% gain, meeting expectations.
On an annual basis, headline PPI accelerated 6.5%, up 0.2 percentage point for the highest annual rate since November 2022.
The report comes just a few weeks ahead of the Federal Reserve's next policy meeting Dec. 8-9. Markets are fully pricing in a quarter percentage point increase in the central bank's key overnight borrowing rate, with slight odds that the Federal Open Market Committee might opt for a half-point hike.
Stock market futures added to gains following the release while Treasury yields were mixed.
Earlier this week, the BLS reported that inflation at the cash register was hotter than expected.
The headline consumer price index saw a 0.4% increase in October while core was up 0.3%, both 0.1 percentage point higher than expected. Because of the government shutdown in October 2025, the BLS couldn't collect some data and refrained from putting out a 12-month inflation figure for CPI.
However, the figures showed that the Fed remains a good distance from its 2% inflation goal.
"Today's PPI data – which shows some signs of improving, albeit still too-high – is unlikely to change the Fed's approach in December because the CPI data was already outside their comfort zone," said Chris Zaccarelli, chief investment officer for Northlight Asset Management.
Moreover, policymakers are beginning to worry that inflation generated by the Iran war and higher fuel prices, along with President Donald Trump's tariffs, are beginning to spread through the economy. The Fed generally would look through such price pressures as temporary, but the breadth of inflation could indicate that inflation is becoming more entrenched.
"We've had some signs of trouble now for several months in a row," Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said in a CNBC interview Friday. "If you look at how broad-based the inflation is, it's not just that we're above the target and have been for some time. It's that in categories that are not driven by oil prices and not driven by tariffs, you're still seeing stalled progress and in some cases going the wrong way."
Stripping out food, energy and trade services, PPI saw an increase of 0.5% in October.
Goods prices increased 0.5% in October, with more than 60% of that move driven by goods excluding food and energy, which actually saw a 0.1% decrease. On an annual basis, the goods index jumped 10.2%, the biggest 12-month surge since October 2022.
Final demand services prices increased 0.2%, most of which was linked to transportation and warehousing services, and within that category a 3.9% gain in truck transportation of freight.
"We've been above 2% for almost six years, and while it sometimes we were making progress, lately we're not making any progress, and if anything, it's going the wrong way," Goolsbee said. "Inflation is rising; it's it's proved far more persistent than we predicted at the beginning from the supply shocks."
Other items in the PPI report also showed multi-year gains. Prices for intermediate processed goods soared 14.6% from October 2025, the biggest annual gain since July 2022. Intermediate prices for services posted a 6.9% increase, the most since November 2022.

articles.title_orig: Russia hit by second car bomb in as many days as peace talks continue
articles.title_zh: Russia hit by second car bomb in as many days as peace talks continue
articles.content_orig:
A car explosion in southern Moscow injured a former aide to a pro-Russian Ukrainian politician on Friday, according to Russian authorities, the second apparent attack in two days.
Sergey Zavorotny, who served as an adviser to the former pro-Russian prime minister of Ukraine Mykola Azarov, was transported to a city hospital for medical care, the Investigative Committee of Russia for the city of Moscow said in a statement.
Azarov served as the Ukrainian prime minister from 2010 to 2014, when he fled to Russia during the street protests known as the Maidan Revolution .
The Russian Investigative Committee said that a comprehensive investigation into the explosion on Moscow’s Kirovogradskaya Street is underway.
Video from the scene shows a dark gray SUV that has been heavily damaged, with the windows apparently blown out.
It’s the latest in a series of apparent attacks or assassinations against political and military figures inside Russia. On Thursday, a car explosion in St. Petersburg killed a Russian serviceman, the local Investigative Committee said.
Russia has blamed Ukraine for earlier assassinations of military officials.
Ukrainian authorities have not commented on this week’s explosions.
The latest incidents come amid the United States’ latest diplomatic efforts to end Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met with both Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Russia’s Vladimir Putin this week, and announced that European delegates will join the next round of peace talks .
The pair had flown to Moscow after trilateral talks between the US, Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi this week concluded with no clear breakthrough.
After speaking to Putin in Moscow, Kushner said: “Both sides have now agreed to expand the next round of negotiations to include our European partners.”
This is a developing story and will be updated.
