articles.title_orig: Alice Huang-Linked Firm Procured Banned Nvidia Chips in China
articles.title_zh: Alice Huang-Linked Firm Procured Banned Nvidia Chips in China
articles.content_orig:
Singapore, a hub for billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia sales each year, finds itself increasingly in the crosshairs of Washington's push to stop advanced AI chips from reaching China, as the chipmaker CEO's scandal once again thrusts the city-state into the spotlight.
The Southeast Asian nation said Thursday that it had barred Alice Huang, the businesswoman at the center of a scandal that catalyzed the end of Jensen Huang's run as Nvidia CEO, from re-entering the country.
A fifth person was handed 41 charges on Friday in a Singapore fraud case involving computer servers that might have contained Nvidia chips and were exported to Malaysia. The alleged transactions in the broader case totaled about $390 million, prosecutors said March last year.
The investigations into several companies and key officials, including Megaspeed International, began in February 2025 and remained ongoing as of Thursday.
Authorities have been examining whether servers exported through Singapore to Malaysia without entering the domestic market were subsequently rerouted to another destination, contrary to declarations made in Singapore, the Ministry of Home Affairs said in a statement late Thursday.
Singapore has faced growing international scrutiny, particularly from the U.S., over its role as a major billing and potential transit hub for Nvidia chips that U.S. officials say have reached China.
The U.S. has imposed export restrictions on Nvidia's most cutting-edge AI chips to China since 2022 to curb Beijing's surging AI development.
Nvidia's revenue linked to Singapore rose to 22% in the fiscal quarter ending July 2025, up from 8% in 2023, with the country's trade ministry estimating chips physically delivered there accounted for less than 1% of the chipmaker's revenue.
Experts have pointed to gaps in enforcement of U.S. export restrictions and Singapore's corporate system that make it hard to trace where advanced Nvidia chips ultimately end up.
Nvidia chips can be legally sold to customers in other countries, such as Malaysia or Singapore, and then illicitly resold or re-exported to China. Chinese companies can also legally gain remote access to the most advanced AI chips hosted in data centers outside China rather than buying the hardware directly.
Chris McGuire, a senior fellow at Council on Foreign Relations and former U.S. national security official, said that Southeast Asia has become "a major hub for chip smuggling and export control circumvention," importing tens of billions of dollars' worth of AI chips per year.
Singapore has stepped up efforts to police suspected chip diversion since last year, including investigations involving alleged fraud and money laundering.
Authorities acknowledged the potential "blind spots between separate monitoring of trade flows and banking flows," said Alvin Camba, lead scientist and director of research at Lyvi, an Austin-based AI risk assessment firm. Correlating physical shipments with related financial transactions can be "challenging," he added.
"Singapore's strong corporate secrecy regulations, which offer extensive protections for foreign investors, can also make it difficult to rapidly identify the true recipients of goods," Camba said.
Those challenges can be exploited to "obfuscate financial flows and potentially circumvent global restrictions on technology transfers," he added, urging constant adaptation from regulators.
Singapore said it had received limited help from U.S. authorities in its yearlong investigation.
Police sought information on Super Micro Computer Inc., a U.S. server supplier relevant to the probe, but the company provided limited cooperation, according to the Thursday statement.
The city-state first raised the issue with U.S. authorities in July 2025, and has repeated its request on several occasions since September last year. "Despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance in respect of the company," it said.
Police interviewed Alice Huang, a Hong Kong resident who was then Megaspeed's CEO, chairperson and a key controller, in June 2025.
In February 2026, authorities concluded that there was insufficient evidence that she had committed offenses related to the declarations under investigation. She was nonetheless barred from re-entering Singapore after being found providing inaccurate information to downplay her role in Megaspeed.
The country does not enforce "unilateral export controls" imposed by other countries, the ministry said in Thursday's statement, but it expects companies operating there to take foreign export rules into account in their international business activities.
Megaspeed, which was spun off from a Chinese gaming company, became Nvidia's largest Southeast Asian customer in less than three years and has bought more than $4.8 billion worth of its chips since June 2024, according to The New York Times, though the company has denied any wrongdoing.
Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence identified as a Chinese intelligence asset passing information to Beijing, served as managing director at Megaspeed for eight months in 2023 but has reportedly continued to play a leading role at the company.
Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia CEO on Thursday, ending 33 years at the helm after revelations that he had two extramarital affairs, plunging the chipmaker at the heart of the global AI boom into crisis.
Nvidia appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while its board searches for a permanent successor.

articles.title_orig: Widespread Microsoft Outage Roils Businesses, Governments and More
articles.title_zh: Widespread Microsoft Outage Roils Businesses, Governments and More
articles.content_orig:
Police forces, hospitals, GP surgeries and councils across the south of England have been sharing advice and updates after a global Microsoft outage left them without email access.
Most say they are continuing to operate as normal but some online forms and electronic-based services are not working and there may be delays to enquiries.
The region's three police forces - Hampshire & Isle of Wight, Thames Valley and Dorset - all said their phone lines were working and they were able to respond to emergencies but their online reporting systems were down.
Hospitals have asked outpatients to attend booked appointments, adding there was no need to check they were going ahead.
Microsoft 365 Services, including Teams, Outlook and Microsoft's artificial intelligence software Copilot, have been affected by "connectivity problems" .
Microsoft has said the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident, but efforts to fix the issues on Friday had so far been unsuccessful.
In a Facebook update on Friday morning, Dorset Police said: "We are currently unable to receive online form submissions. Until this is resolved, if your report is time-critical but not an emergency, please dial 101.
"If your report can wait until Microsoft restores its service, please submit an online form once you are able to do so."
Hampshire police sought to allay fears about the effect of the outage on services.
It said: "We can confirm that our ability to answer and respond to 999 and 101 calls has not been impacted by the widely reported issues with Microsoft.
"We know that the current situation will be causing concern... but our ability to respond to emergencies has not been compromised."
Isle of Wight NHS Trust said its emergency services remained operational through the outage and teams had "established plans in place to minimise disruption and maintain safe patient care".
It said: "If your enquiry is urgent, please contact the relevant service by telephone rather than email where possible."
Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust said: "Our services remain operational, but there may be delays in responding to enquiries.
"If you need to contact us, please telephone us rather than email.
"If you have an appointment with us, please attend as planned. There is no need to contact us to confirm your appointment."
Tower House GP surgery in Ryde said the outage could affect some of its services, with delays responding to online consultations, hospital letters and discharge documents.
It said it was prioritising urgent clinical matters and patient safety.
Slough Borough Council in Berkshire said staff at its customer service centre who usually dealt with email enquiries had been transferred onto the phones but urged people only to call if their request was urgent because lines were expected to be busy.
East Hampshire District Council said its emails were down but residents registered on its MyEHDC system could still use the general enquiries form.
Lyme Regis Town Council in Dorset said it was using a mobile phone number for urgent issues because its telephone lines were also affected and working intermittently.

articles.title_orig: Ancient tunnels beneath famous Hagia Sophia explored after 3,000 tons of debris cleared
articles.title_zh: Ancient tunnels beneath famous Hagia Sophia explored after 3,000 tons of debris cleared
articles.content_orig:
Archaeologists have cleared roughly 3,000 tons of debris from ancient Roman tunnels beneath Istanbul's Hagia Sophia, gaining access to previously buried passages beneath the historic landmark.
Archaeologists have removed roughly 3,000 tons of debris from a centuries-old network of underground tunnels beneath Istanbul's iconic Hagia Sophia — revealing previously inaccessible passages beneath one of the world's most historic religious landmarks.
The findings were announced by archaeologist Hasan Fırat Diker at a presentation this fall in Istanbul, as local outlet Türkiye Today reported.
The tunnels have been undergoing excavation and clearing work since February 2025, allowing researchers to explore sections that were previously buried beneath mud and debris.
NOAH'S ARK SITE YIELDS FIRST LOOK AT CHARRED WOOD FRAGMENTS RECOVERED DEEP BELOW SOIL
During the Oct. 16 presentation, Diker said the roughly 1,600-year-old tunnels were built by the Romans and originally functioned as part of the city's water distribution and drainage network, while also providing a protected underground space.
Some of the underground structures predate the present-day Hagia Sophia, which was completed in 537 A.D. under Byzantine Emperor Justinian I.
Archaeologists have removed roughly 3,000 tons of debris from ancient tunnels beneath Istanbul's Hagia Sophia (seen here during a 2022 excavation), revealing previously inaccessible passages. (Isa Terli/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images)
Although the underground network has been known for decades, much of it has remained difficult to access, and the ongoing excavation work is allowing researchers to examine previously buried sections of the historic site .
Diker's research has shed new light on the intricate network, which he compared to a modern subway system, Türkiye Today said.
'DIG OF THE CENTURY' BENEATH NOTRE DAME REVEALS MYSTERIOUS MARKINGS, ANCIENT SECRETS
The tunnels were designed to carry rainwater from surrounding streets into the sea, according to Diker.
Researchers have cleared nearly 558 feet of an underground route connected to a fifth-century Roman street, which extends from the Sarayburnu area toward Little Hagia Sophia, Diker said.
Some underground structures beneath Hagia Sophia predate the current landmark, which was completed in 537 A.D. under Byzantine Emperor Justinian I. (Isa Terli/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images; Prisma/UIG/Getty Images)
The landmark, part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site and visited by millions of tourists each year, is actually the third structure built at the site, Diker said.

He said his team had cleared both the upper and lower sections of an ancient underground burial complex discovered in 1946, excavating an additional five feet beneath it.
The burial chambers predate the current Hagia Sophia; they had accumulated large amounts of mud over the centuries, according to Diker.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS
Looking ahead, Diker said researchers hope to open more sections of Hagia Sophia's underground network to visitors, with plans for an exhibition showcasing the archaeological remains.
Hagia Sophia, one of Istanbul's most historic religious landmarks, sits above an extensive network of Roman-era tunnels and underground structures. (Yasin Akgul/AFP via Getty Images)
Hagia Sophia — which means "Holy Wisdom" in Greek — served as a major center of Eastern Christianity for nearly 1,000 years until Ottoman forces conquered then-Constantinople and converted the church into a mosque in 1453.
It later became a museum in 1935 before being converted back into a mosque in 2020.

The excavation is the latest in a series of archaeological investigations involving ancient underground tunnels around the world.
Researchers have cleared upper and lower sections of an ancient underground burial complex discovered in 1946 beneath Istanbul's historic Hagia Sophia. (Isa Terli/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images)
Earlier this year, archaeologists uncovered a mysterious 164-foot-long tunnel in Jerusalem near a site linked to the biblical Kingdom of Judah, though its age and purpose remain unknown.

In Germany, archaeologists discovered a medieval tunnel beneath a prehistoric burial site after initially mistaking its entrance for a grave.

articles.title_orig: Apple should have made the MacBook logo RGB
articles.title_zh: Apple should have made the MacBook logo RGB
articles.content_orig:
The PROLED MacBook Pro’s logo is lit with boring white LEDs. Missed opportunity.
The PROLED MacBook Pro’s logo is lit with boring white LEDs. Missed opportunity.
When Apple CEO John Ternus announced the first touchscreen Mac last month, the biggest reaction in the room wasn’t for the PROLED MacBook Pro ’s OLED touchscreen or the thinner and lighter chassis; it was for the illuminated lid logo. It’s a throwback to the light-up logos on the old MacBooks, which Apple started phasing out in 2015 , and which were completely gone by the 2018 MacBook Air redesign . It’s a nostalgia play, but boy did it work. It’s fun!
Just like in the old days, the new logo’s brightness is linked to the screen’s: The brighter or dimmer the screen, the brighter or dimmer the logo. But the light-up logo on the old MacBooks was illuminated by the screen’s backlight, and an OLED display doesn’t have one. Thanks to iFixit , we now know it’s lit by four white LEDs and synced with the screen’s brightness by software. But that means Apple could have used RGB LEDs.
Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet, or anything in between? On the lid of your new MacBook Pro? Why not? After all, Apple insists it’s still serious about gaming , and nothing says “serious about gaming” like RGB lighting.
I was secretly hoping users would be able to customize the illuminated lid cutout much like the Xbox logo on Microsoft’s Elite Series 2 controllers . But alas, no luck. You can turn off the illumination with some Terminal commands or take control of it with a third-party app. But when it’s lit, it’s only lit with white light. And iFixit’s teardown also showed the difficulty of accessing those LEDs (the screen delaminated and broke in the process). So we’re unlikely to see LED RGB mods for it unless someone’s brave enough to void their warranty and risk a pricey screen repair on their $3,000 laptop.
The most fun you can have with the Apple lid logo is to install a free third-party app like LogoLight and have it pulse, breathe, match the beat of any music you’re playing, or flash some Morse code. There’s some fun there, but if you combined these features with a splash of color we’d really be cooking.
MacBooks aren’t gaming laptops, so RGB lighting may seem like a mismatch, but multicolor LEDs could have been a cool Easter egg. Nobody thought Apple would put a touchscreen on a MacBook either, and the iPhone Duo and HomeView also show Apple is in a new age of experimentation during the early Ternus era. Maybe if the light-up lid logo ever comes to future MacBook Airs or a MacBook Neo, Apple could cut loose a little.

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang didn’t show confidence in his successor, report says
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang didn’t show confidence in his successor, report says
articles.content_orig:
Former NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang described Colette Kress, the company’s CFO who has now replaced him as interim CEO, as “a deer in the headlights” during a presentation earlier in the summer, the Wall Street Journal reported , citing an anonymous source.
Huang made the comment during a meeting with Nvidia’s finance team about the company’s plans to provide guarantees worth billions of dollars to data center operators that couldn’t afford to buy its chips upfront, according to the report.
He reportedly also said Kress was a person who couldn’t help him steer strategy or decision-making.
Kress has been with Nvidia for over 13 years now, after serving as SVP and CFO of Cisco’s Business Technology Operations Finance. The report said she has questioned Nvidia’s program-focused, credit-based deals involving Huang’s son-in-law Nico Caprez, and wanted to know how to decide which deals are beneficial, how to value guarantees, and determine returns.
Earlier in the year, she had scaled back on Nvidia’s commitment for OpenAI’s ambitious Ohio data center project. The company was in talks to provide $250 billion in credit to OpenAI, but ended up committing $105 billion .
Huang resigned Thursday after reports of two extramarital affairs , including one with the company’s VP for healthcare, Kimberly Powell. The company is also investigating a possible Chinese espionage plot .
After his resignation, Reuters reported that he was having a third affair with another employee . Nvidia is currently searching for a permanent CEO to replace Huang, who had the top job for over 33 years.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft says November security updates cause printing issues
articles.title_zh: Microsoft says November security updates cause printing issues
articles.content_orig:
According to a Microsoft service alert that Bleeping Computer discovered, "After installing the November 2026 Windows security update (the Originating KBs listed above), or later updates, printing might fail for documents containing images rendered with a height or width value of zero at the selected printing resolution."
"These images can be used as part of certain complex document formatting, such as adding "invisible" images intended to serve as a document watermark, layout anchoring, or generation tools that may inserting images objects even when no graphic present."
When you attempt to print on Windows , the document can contain these invisible images even when the user hasn't inserted any of their own image. Formatting and document-generation tools may add these elements as you attempt to print; meaning, you can't tell if the document will print properly, even if it looks perfect on your end. The printing error affects devices running Windows 10 or later and Windows Server 2016 or later, meaning the problem affects both personal and business computers.
The new bug appeared just as Microsoft patched printer errors that earlier 2025 updates introduced, including a bug that made USB printers produce random text in March, followed by a fix for the broken "Print to PDF" feature introduced in the July update. It also fixed a bug from the October update that prevented users from adding Active Directory printers through Settings, producing error 87.
Alongside the regular Tuesday patch, Microsoft also introduced a Windows 11 Insider preview that contained a set of additional smaller features, such as the option to disable the annoying "sticky keys" option forever .
Microsoft also disclosed new bugs affecting automated Windows activation and licensing, and users of the Software Licensing Management Tool (SLMGR) command-line tool. These bugs display the error code '0x80041008'.
"Affected devices might encounter error 0x80041008, Invalid parameter (SWbemObjectEx), when running commands to activate Windows, configure Key Management Service (KMS), or manage product keys,"
"Devices that are being configured to use KMS activation might encounter errors when attempting to initiate their activation. KMS-activated devices typically remain activated for up to 180 days following successful activation," Microsoft states in its alert.
The issue occurs when running either slmgr.vbs /skms-domain or slmgr.vbs /ipk on Windows 10 versions 21H2 and 22H2, Windows 11 version 23H2, or Windows Server 2019, 2022, and 2025.
Microsoft assures customers that the bug won't affect pre-existing users with the KMS client key installed, stating, "Devices that are already activated remain activated. Customers whose devices already have the appropriate KMS client key and KMS configuration, and who do not need to run the affected Slmgr.vbs commands, are not expected to be affected."
Microsoft says a fix for the licensing issues should arrive in the coming days. Until then, organizations needing immediate assistance should contact Microsoft Support for business. Finally, as of right now, Microsoft Outlook is on the second day of experiencing widespread outages . Microsoft is expecting to fix the problem soon.
Source: Bleeping Computer via Microsoft

articles.title_orig: Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Sells 5 Million in Four Days, Yet Former Nintendo Leads Say The Series Sold “Like Nothing” Before Breath of the Wild
articles.title_zh: Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Sells 5 Million in Four Days, Yet Former Nintendo Leads Say The Series Sold “Like Nothing” Before Breath of the Wild
articles.content_orig:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has become a smashing success, selling over 5 million copies in only four days of availability, but the Nintendo Switch 2 remake of one of the best games ever released had the real risk of never seeing the light of day. According to former Nintendo of America marketing leads Kit Ellis and Krysta Yang , the franchise was going through its darkest days before the launch of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild , with new games selling like nothing.
"The series was in dire straits. They were selling like nothing," said Yang during the latest episode of the Kit & Krysta Podcast . "Yeah, I remember I was going to the focus groups. It was a really dark moment," added Ellis . "The feedback is the fan base is dwindling, this is not bringing in new players. We had so much data of like every game, the interest in the audience was getting smaller and smaller. They had to do something drastic."
Looking at the timeline, it's very likely that The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword contributed a lot to the dark age of the franchise, which required the massive open-world overhaul of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild . The first 3D entry in the series built from the ground up for the Wii system sold only 3.67 million units, a disappointing figure considering the 101 million Wii systems sold worldwide. Making this figure even more dire is how the Nintendo Switch HD remaster released in 2021 outsold the original in just a few months, benefiting from the massive popularity of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild .
With The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake enjoying such incredible popularity, it will be interesting to see where Eiji Aonuma and his team will take the franchise. While both Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom are incredible games, they can sometimes feel too big, a feeling that's highlighted well by the immaculate pacing of the Ocarina of Time remake, granted by the great design of Hyrule . Regardless of which direction will define the next era of the franchise, there's no denying that the dark days are indeed over for Link and Zelda .
About the author : Francesco De Meo has been covering video games and technology since 2012, starting his career at small outlets like Gamersyndrome and GeekSnack. 

After joining the Wccftech gaming section in 2015, he quickly expanded his video gaming coverage with in-depth reporting, interviews with iconic industry figures such as Grasshopper Manufacture founder and No More Heroes creator Goichi "Suda51" Suda, Resident Evil series creator Shinji Mikami, Team NINJA's president and Nioh series director Fumihiko Yasuda, and Silent Hill creator Keiichiro Toyama, reviews and on-the-ground coverage of major industry events such as Gamescom and E3.

When he's not reporting or reviewing, Francesco can be found playing the genres he loves most, spending time with his six cats, reading, writing music, playing guitar and drumming for his progressive rock band.

articles.title_orig: Eleanor Donaldson given supervision order and placed on sex offenders' register
articles.title_zh: Eleanor Donaldson given supervision order and placed on sex offenders' register
articles.content_orig:
Judge imposes three-year treatment order on Donaldson for aiding and abetting sexual offences by her husband, Jeffrey
Jeffrey Donaldson’s wife, Eleanor, has been placed on the sex offender register for five years for aiding and abetting sexual offences by her disgraced husband.
Eleanor Donaldson appeared via remote link at Newry crown court to hear the order on Friday one month after her husband, the former Democratic Unionist party ( DUP ) leader, was convicted of abusing two women when they were children.
The 60-year-old bowed her head and cried as Judge Paul Ramsey imposed a three-year supervision and treatment order as well as placing her on the sex offender register. Asked if she understood the court order, she nodded and said yes.
In June her husband was convicted of 18 sexual offences , including one count of rape, spanning 1985 to 2008. The case stunned Northern Ireland and destroyed the career and reputation of a politician who had been the leading voice of unionism. In October he was sentenced to 15 years .
His wife faced a trial of the facts after being deemed unfit to participate in a conventional trial on mental health grounds. A jury found that she had aided and abetted her husband’s abuse.
She could not be given a prison sentence, only a hospital order, a supervised treatment order or a discharge. Two experts, one for the prosecution and one for the defence, told the court that a supervised treatment order was the most appropriate option.
The victims, known as complainants A and B, were in court for the hearing on Friday. The prosecutor, Rosemary Walsh KC, told the court that “pain permeated” their statements.
Donaldson’s three-minute appearance on screen was the first time she had been seen in court since 2025. Wearing a black jumper, and with close-cropped hair and two cuts on her forehead, she cast her eyes down and held a tissue.
The judge told the court the medical evidence about her was unchallenged and that a supervision and treatment order was “inevitable”. Donaldson would be under the supervision of a social worker from the Craigavon community mental health team for three years, he said.
This would require attending appointments, treatment and home visits, said Ramsey. She will be subject to the notification provisions of the sex offender register for five years.
Bronagh Muldoon, the assistant director for the National Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Children Northern Ireland, said aiding and abetting abuse required consequences.
“It is right and important that the role she played in these terrible crimes has been recognised in court today. The women involved in this case have shown incredible bravery in coming forward to ensure the Donaldsons have both been held accountable,” Muldoon said.
The former DUP leader is appealing against his convictions and his wife is appealing against the jury verdict.

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang’s years-long effort to get close to China
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang’s years-long effort to get close to China
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.
Nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.
"Although we expect the company to fulfill all of its previously announced commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate new multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider said in a note Thursday.
The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.
Tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.
On Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.77%, nearly 6% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.
Tech stocks slumped Thursday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 0.3% as markets digested the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Thursday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt  lingers.
It's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The company had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.
Neoclouds CoreWeave , Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.
CoreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.75% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped 18% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.
It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, said CreditSights analyst Andy Li.
"We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he said.
"However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.
CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday , before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person."
"There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my company every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he said in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us."
Bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any big changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.
The real issue is just how much money the company will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.
"Big companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he said. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies."
— CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: EXCLUSIVE: Huang exit and US scrutiny imperil $3 billion in Chinese AI projects reliant on Nvidia
articles.title_zh: EXCLUSIVE: Huang exit and US scrutiny imperil $3 billion in Chinese AI projects reliant on Nvidia
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia 's leadership crisis is creating an opening for its biggest rivals, as investors bet that Jensen Huang's departure could loosen the AI chip giant's grip on an industry it has long dominated.
From AMD to Broadcom and even partner TSMC , chipmakers are emerging as potential beneficiaries of the upheaval, with market watchers pointing to a possible redistribution of manufacturing capacity and a narrowing of Nvidia's technological lead.
"What you're seeing in markets now is a bit of a rotation into other advanced chip design companies, on the assumption that this will enable other companies effectively to catch up," said Mark Franklin, head of multi-asset solutions for Asia at Manulife Investment Management.
That shift comes as Nvidia grapples with the fallout from Huang's resignation, following revelations about his multiple affairs including with a woman believed by the U.S. intelligence community to be a Chinese spy .
Huang's departure could give competitors an opportunity to close the gap as Nvidia navigates leadership uncertainty, Franklin highlighted, adding that the rotation was already helping fuel positive momentum in other semiconductor stocks.
Farzin Azam, managing director of equities trading at Mizuho Americas, said the shift was evident on trading desks, with investors moving toward chipmakers less exposed to Nvidia's management turmoil.
"Names such as TSMC, names such as Broadcom, names such as Advanced Micro will come as winners of this because they don't have this overhang of a management disruption," Azam told CNBC.
Nvidia shares have plunged 11% so far this week, while rivals AMD and Broadcom have gained 30% and 24%, respectively.
TSMC, which manufactures Nvidia's most advanced processors, has also rallied 11% over the same period, as it stands to benefit , irrespective of which chip designer gains or loses. A rotation away from AI names perceived as risky also positions TSMC as a relatively safer play for those bullish on the overall theme.
The rotation away from Nvidia has also extended into less speculative corners of the semiconductor industry, including analog chipmakers such as Texas Instruments, Analog Devices and Infineon, as investors adopt a more defensive stance, he said.
Texas Instruments has climbed about 13% this week, while Analog Devices and Germany's Infineon have advanced 12% and 14%, respectively.
Beyond the immediate market reaction, Huang's exit could fundamentally reshape competition across the AI supply chain, according to Dylan Patel, chief executive at semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis.
Patel said Huang had personally cultivated relationships with manufacturers and component suppliers, helping Nvidia secure scarce production capacity ahead of rivals.
That advantage could now come under pressure as companies including Google and Amazon strive to expand AI chip production.
The two hyperscalers were already gaining ground in securing supply-chain capacity relative to Nvidia, Patel said, and could accelerate those efforts without Huang's influence over suppliers.
"If Nvidia can't muster the supply chain, then technology is the only competitive advantage. And without Jensen, can they maintain technology advantages? Given they're only a year ahead of their biggest competitors, it's not like the gap is massive," Patel said.
The challenge is particularly acute as hyperscalers increasingly develop proprietary AI chips to reduce their reliance on Nvidia, while AMD and other semiconductor companies race to capture a larger slice of the market.
Yet the upheaval doesn't necessarily signal an end to the broader AI investment boom.
Franklin noted that major technology companies are projecting higher AI spending in 2027, with further increases possible in 2028, signaling the investment cycle remains structurally intact even as investors reassess which companies stand to benefit.
The bigger question is whether growing competition and the proliferation of open-source technologies eventually commoditize AI capabilities, putting pressure on chip prices and investment returns, he said.
For Nvidia, the immediate outlook may depend less on its earnings than on whether its next leadership team can reassure investors.
Azam said the stock appeared inexpensive relative to its earnings growth prospects, but warned that ongoing investigations and management uncertainty could limit any sustained recovery.
He expects Nvidia's earnings due Nov. 17 to remain strong, with investors likely to focus more closely on management's plans for navigating the crisis.
The result could be a reshuffling of winners within the semiconductor industry, with Franklin saying that investors were becoming more comfortable staying invested while rotating and diversifying their portfolios, instead of abandoning the market altogether.

articles.title_orig: How the Microsoft outage has been felt worldwide
articles.title_zh: How the Microsoft outage has been felt worldwide
articles.content_orig:
At least 74 countries have been affected by the Microsoft outage since it was detected after midday US Eastern Time (17:00 GMT) on Thursday.
Microsoft 365 Services, including Teams, Outlook and artificial intelligence software Copilot, were experiencing "connectivity problems", the company said.
As of 12:00 GMT on Friday, it reported seeing "encouraging recovery progress in Europe" while Japan remained "comparatively more stable" and North America was "also improving".
From city governments in the US to Australian spy agencies, the disruption has been widespread. Here's what's been happening around the world.
In the US , staff with the House of Representatives told Politico their work had been halted by the outage.
"We all use Outlook, that's our life, everything is there, our calendar is there, our boss's calendar, so it has been a challenge … with no access to our Bible," one House staff member said. "There goes a day of legislative work."
Tech giants OpenAI and Anthropic have both reported problems.
OpenAI, which makes ChatGPT, said it was investigating an issue affecting its connections to Microsoft's services, which caused some tools not to work as expected.
Courts from Los Angeles to Texas also warned that communications might be delayed.
Electric truck maker Workhorse Group, which was expected to report third-quarter results on 12 November, rescheduled to 16 November, citing business disruptions caused by the outage.
Meanwhile, officials in some US cities encouraged citizens to call local offices and agencies where needed instead of using email.
The City of Austin in Texas account posted on X early on Friday: "Due to an ongoing Microsoft Outlook outage, City of Austin employees cannot receive or send emails at this time.
"City phone lines remain operational, and 911 Emergency services are not impacted."
In Canada , a healthcare network running several hospitals in Toronto had declared a "code grey", indicating an infrastructure failure.
The company, Unity Health Toronto, said its teams were having trouble sending or receiving email but that patient care was not affected.
Other hospitals, including Canada's largest children's hospital SickKids, also reported its staff having issues accessing phone calls and emails.
Via Rail, Canada's national train network, said in a post on X that its passengers may not be able to receive emails about their trips due to the outage.
Disruptions have also been reported by Canadian municipalities, including the City of Ottawa and the City of Vancouver. Both urged residents in a notice to call in for any urgent issues.
In Japan , some companies reportedly turned to fax machines to maintain communications.
"Can't send emails because of a Microsoft outage, so we're switching to fax for the regular updates we usually send as PDFs. Analog is strong," one unnamed X user was quoted as saying by the Japan Times .
The Japanese government said its shared IT platform had been disrupted.
"We understand that Microsoft is working to restore services, and we will continue to monitor the company's response," Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary Masanao Ozaki told reporters.
Singapore also confirmed the outage had affected some government systems, but stressed "emergency services remain fully operational".
Singapore's courts also said they were "experiencing issues with incoming and outgoing emails", urging people to contact them by telephone for urgent matters.
In the Philippines , the Supreme Court warned that "responses to emails and other transactions may be delayed".
In India , the outage was disrupting work for many on Friday, with emails not landing and Teams calls not going through smoothly.
People working in the equity markets told BBC News they had panicked when they realised they could not access daily research reports before their morning meeting where they make their big decisions of the day.
"Outlook wasn't working. We fortunately have an alternative so it was not a problem. But we conduct most of our calls, especially with big clients, on Teams - that has been a challenge," a senior executive with a big Indian brokerage said on condition of anonymity.
Firms in China use software that has been made locally - WPS Office is a favourite - but the Microsoft outage caused frustration there too.
Outlook is one of the few reliable channels for many offices and businesses in the country who work with colleagues across the world.
China operates one of the world's most sophisticated systems of internet censorship, known as the Great Firewall, which restricts access to many Western websites including Google, Facebook and Instagram along with many international news organisations including the BBC.
Australia's spy and federal police agencies have been affected by the outage, though officials have suggested the impact is minimal.
"The impact that they are dealing with is very much on email system", the head of the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation, Mike Burgess, told reporters.
Other Australian public service providers also confirmed they had been affected by the outage, but similarly said this was mostly limited to emails, and the BBC understands there were no major impacts across New South Wales' primary services in health, education, transport, and emergency services.
European stock market operator Euronext advised listed companies on Friday morning to use the phone to communicate corporate information because of the Outlook email disruption, Reuters reported.
In the UK , GPs, police and pharmacies are among services affected.
Some GP surgeries have urged patients not to submit messages via their website while the problem remains, while several large police forces are urging members of the public to call if they want to make a report.
Politicians are also affected. At Westminster, MPs were reporting their access via parliamentary accounts to Microsoft products was down.
A parliamentary spokesperson said: "We are aware of the global issue affecting Microsoft email services, which is impacting users of the parliamentary network. We are working with Microsoft to resolve the matter as quickly as possible.
"Alternative communication arrangements are in place, allowing today's business to continue."
Some parts of Asia, Europe and Africa remain unaffected, according to Downdetector. These include Russia, where the use of Microsoft applications is heavily restricted, or phased out in favour of domestic alternatives.
However, this could also be a case of under-reporting in some countries, where Downdetector is among the websites blocked due to censorship.

articles.title_orig: Israeli strike on Gaza’s Nasser Hospital kills at least six people, officials say
articles.title_zh: Israeli strike on Gaza’s Nasser Hospital kills at least six people, officials say
articles.content_orig:
An Israeli airstrike on a hospital in southern Gaza overnight killed at least six people, the Health Ministry in the Palestinian enclave said Thursday.
The strike hit a surgery building at Nasser Hospital, with medical staff and patients among those killed, including a surgeon and a 13-year-old boy, health officials said. The Israeli military said it was targeting a Hamas commander and other militants.
The strike — the latest despite an ongoing U.S.-backed ceasefire — shattered ceilings and left debris strewn across wards inside the hospital, which is one of the few functioning medical facilities left in Gaza after the destruction of Israel’s yearslong military assault.
Palestinian surgeon Dr. Rizk Abu Shaira was among those killed, the Health Ministry said. He was featured in the 2026 documentary “American Doctor,” which followed three American doctors helping to provide medical care in Gaza.
An array of munitions debris was displayed at the hospital site as media visited on Thursday. Two munitions experts said an image supplied to NBC News appeared to show debris from a GBU-39 Small Diameter Bomb. The U.S. is known to supply Israel with GBU-39 munitions, which are produced by Boeing in the United States and sold to a number of countries.
The IDF and Pentagon did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether U.S.-manufactured munitions were used in the strike. While the image was captured at Nasser Hospital following the strike, NBC News is not able to independently confirm that they were the munitions used in the attack or how they came to be displayed there.
Justin Bronk, a senior research fellow for airpower and technology in the military sciences at the Royal United Services Institute, a think tank based in London, said he made that determination based on the “wing section visible,” adding that the GBU-39 “is a U.S. supplied weapon.”
Brian Castner, a crisis researcher at Amnesty International, also identified the munitions as belonging to a GBU-39, adding that Israel has used the bomb “in many strikes in Gaza.”
Sam Lair, a fellow at the Foreign Policy Research Institute who manages and conducts investigations into nuclear and missile programs, said NBC News’ imagery appeared inconclusive, but “the wings, tail actuation system, lugs, and warhead” shown in other photos appear to match “a GBU-39 series small diameter bomb.”
“It looks to be some kind of glide bomb or cruise missile, and the English on the frame suggests it could be U.S.-origin, but I don’t see anything conclusive,” he said.
Dr. Ayman Abu Obeid, head of the surgery department at Nasser Hospital, said there was no “notice, warning or anything” before the hospital was attacked. “Suddenly, there was fire and shelling and walls were brought down instantly,” he said.
He said he was not aware of any “resistance fighters or combatants present — only a medical team treating patients.”
NBC News also spoke with two surgeons who travelled to Gaza from the U.K. earlier this month to assist with medical care, and were said were in the hospital when the missile struck.
Both Dr. Goher Rahbour, a consultant general and colorectal surgeon, and Dr. Stephan Verborg, a limb reconstruction surgeon, said they were also not aware of any warning from the Israeli military before the strike, which hit the hospital shortly after midnight.
“I heard the impact and I felt the explosion because the whole hospital shook,” Verborg said in a phone interview Thursday. He said he was about 15 to 20 meters away from the point of impact, adding: “You could smell the smoke. You could see the dust.”
Rahbour said he had been operating with Abu Shaira, whom he described as a “lovely” and “affable” person, earlier that day. He said they had been laughing and joking together Wednesday evening in the hours just before the Palestinian surgeon was killed.
Both doctors had traveled to Gaza early this month through the organization IDEALS, a U.K. charity seeking to provide sustainable humanitarian aid to regions affected by conflict or natural disasters. They said they had not seen any indication of a Hamas presence in the hospital.
Tributes were paid to Abu Shaira. “Dr. Rizq was at the hospital during the entire war,” Dr. Mohammed Zaqout, director general of the Health Ministry in Gaza, could be seen telling a crowd of mourners, surrounding a body covered in a shroud, in a video captured for NBC News on Thursday. “He didn’t abandon his duties for even one day.”
Nasser Hospital said a 13-year-old boy, identified as Jihad Naeem Muhammad Abu Tilikh, was also among those killed.
The Israeli military and the Israel Security Agency said they struck a senior Hamas member, along with other militants, who they said had “advanced” attacks from the hospital in the southern Gaza Strip overnight. In a later statement, they identified the senior member as Muhammad Abu Ismail, who they said served as the commander of Hamas’ Khan Younis Brigade and had also been responsible for holding hostages in Gaza.
The IDF and ISA said Hamas had “established a presence within the hospital complex and used it as a command center” and stored weapons and conducted interrogations and torture from within the medical complex.
The IDF claimed the hospital’s second floor “serves as a Hamas military HQ, where civilians are not permitted to enter,” alleging that “dozens of hostages were held captive” there earlier in the war. It shared undated photos of weapons that it alleged were found within the complex and others.
The IDF and ISA said steps had been taken to “mitigate harm to civilians, including the use of precision munitions and aerial surveillance.” They also later said “advance warnings were issued to the population.” The IDF said it was looking into reports that medical workers,  including Abu Shaira, and patients were killed.
One woman, Tahani Ibrahim Abu Anza, said her brother, Khaled Abu Anza, was killed in the strike, with Nasser Hospital separately confirming his death.
A number of media outlets, including Israeli media outlet Ynet , reported that a commander in Hamas’ Khan Younis Brigade of that same name was killed in the strike. Asked to confirm that and whether he was directly targeted, the IDF said it would get back on the matter.
Tahani Ibrahim Abu Anza did not directly identify her brother, 53, as a Hamas member, but said she believed he was targeted. He had been at the hospital for physical therapy after undergoing surgery, she said.
“He did not come to the hospital to engage in combat or resistance. He came for medical treatment,” she said.
Hamas condemned the allegations that it was using the hospital for military operations as “lies of the criminal enemy” and called the attack a “war crime.”
Hospitals have protected status under international law, but they have been heavily targeted under Israel’s yearslong offensive in Gaza. The Israeli military has repeatedly accused Hamas of operating within medical facilities, a charge the militant group has denied.
The overnight attack was not the first time that Nasser Hospital itself has been targeted.
In August 2025, the hospital was hit by a double tap Israeli strik e that killed at least 20 people, including journalists and health workers. The deadly attack sparked international outrage.
Of Gaza’s 37 hospitals, just two are considered to be “fully functioning,” while 18 are partially functioning and 17 are considered nonfunctioning after much of the enclave’s healthcare system was devastated under Israel’s offensive, according to data published by the World Health Organization.
Israeli strikes have continued in Gaza despite a ceasefire agreement reached in October of last year.
More than 1,600 people have been killed since the truce came into effect, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry in the enclave. Israel says four of its ⁠soldiers have ​been killed in that time.
Both Israel and Hamas have accused each other of violating the ceasefire.

articles.title_orig: After Xi Purges China’s Generals, a Military Inquisitor Rises
articles.title_zh: After Xi Purges China’s Generals, a Military Inquisitor Rises
articles.content_orig:
When China’s leader, Xi Jinping, endorsed the expulsion of dozens of disgraced officials at a recent Communist Party meeting in Beijing, one man stood out as a clear winner.
Taking his new place at the front of the meeting was Gen. Zhang Shengmin, the somber-faced enforcer of Mr. Xi’s purges inside the military. He had been promoted to the Politburo, the party’s top leadership council, the latest step in his improbable rise from low-profile inspector to a position second only to Mr. Xi in China’s military hierarchy.
General Zhang has been the principal overseer of Mr. Xi’s campaign to purify the People’s Liberation Army. His latest elevation signaled that the investigations, indoctrination drives and loyalty tests could continue for years, as Mr. Xi searches for officers he believes are irreproachably loyal, experts and officials said.
“Twist the blade inward, with strict measures to cure disorder,” China’s main military newspaper said after the party meeting that was held late last month, referring to the continued discipline campaign.
Three officials in Taiwan said they believed Mr. Xi’s loyalty campaign would keep the Chinese military focused on its own problems. That could hinder preparations for possible war over Taiwan, the self-governed island democracy that Beijing claims. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss internal assessments.
The leadership uncertainty comes as China’s military has continued to pressure Taiwan. Dozens of P.L.A. ships held unannounced drills in seas off the Chinese coast in recent weeks, with some, including a carrier strike group, still remaining, Joseph Wu , the secretary-general of Taiwan’s National Security Council, posted on X on Thursday.

articles.title_orig: Trump's reliance on ousted Nvidia CEO in question ahead of China trip
articles.title_zh: Trump's reliance on ousted Nvidia CEO in question ahead of China trip
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Jensen Huang, the billionaire co-founder of tech firm Nvidia, resigned as CEO after allegations of extramarital affairs including with an alleged Chinese spy rocked his company.
The 63-year-old’s departure comes in the wake of a scandal that has wiped an estimated $500 billion off the chipmaker’s market value , with share prices plunging 12 percent to start Thursday. However, they have rebounded some ad were down 5 percent by midday.
One of the world’s richest men, Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993, which is now at the heart of the AI revolution. He is the company’s fourth-largest investor with a stake of about 3.61 percent, and will exit the Nvidia board with immediate effect, the company announced Thursday.
“Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound. Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” Nvidia said in a statement.
U.S. President Donald Trump, who is close to Huang , suggested former Apple CEO Tim Cook should replace him.
“NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple,” Trump posted Thursday on Truth Social. “A Legend replaces a Legend!”
When the board announced Huang’s resignation early Thursday it also stated that Colette Kress, Nvidia’s executive vice president and chief financial officer, would serve as interim CEO.
“The Board, Estaff (executive staff) and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period,” Kress wrote in a memo to employees, adding the company will host a meeting on November 18.
Huang’s problems began when The New York Times reported he had had an affair with former Megaspeed director Alice Huang — no relation — whom U.S. intelligence has said facilitated shipments of Nvidia’s microchips to Chinese firms as part of a foreign intelligence operation.
The newspaper subsequently alleged that the executive had also had a relationship with Kimberly Powell , his company’s vice president of healthcare, who is also married.
After the first of the infidelities was disclosed, the executive sent a memo to Nvidia employees Sunday admitting he had been unfaithful to his wife of 40 years , Lori Huang, and said he was “deeply sorry” for the hurt he had case without going into details. Nvidia’s board responded by launching an internal investigation .
China meanwhile denied the espionage claims, calling them “purely unsubstantiated and directed at smearing China.”
Huang’s exit creates a leadership vacuum at the $4 trillion chipmaker, that is the driving force behind the global AI boom and at the heart of the big tech arms race between the U.S. and China .
For years, Nvidia was best known to video gamers for helping produce top-tier graphics. But its chips' ability to perform many calculations at once has made them a strategic prize in the US-China race to dominate AI technology. It also made Nvidia the world's most valuable company.
The success turned Huang into a rock-star CEO, mobbed by fans in Taiwan and South Korea who would ask him to sign books, posters and even their bodies.
Prior to the announcement, Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, an expert on corporate governance at Yale School of Management, told NBC News the scandal meant Huang had “lost his legitimacy to lead internally in the eyes of the company, and he’s lost his external credibility in the eyes of key constituents, including customers.”
Before the resignation, fellow tech boss Elon Musk said it would be “an honor” to hire Huang, the pair having previously worked together on Tesla, xAI and space-based data center projects.
The world’s richest man recently said of Huang, “old friends are the best friends,” adding: “Jensen rocks.”
It is not yet clear whether Huang’s extramarital affairs will end his marriage. Forbes has estimated Lori Huang could receive a windfall of at least $75 billion if the couple does divorce, putting her in an exclusive tech billionaire ex-wives’ club that also includes Melinda French Gates and MacKenzie Scott.
The scandal has also reverberated in Washington, D.C., with reports that Trump was warned about Huang’s compromised position by Secretary of State Marco Rubio in May when the executive joined their visit to Beijing.
Earlier this week, Trump said he had “absolutely no idea” that the first reported affair was with a suspected Chinese spy.
“I think ​he's an honorable guy," Trump said, adding ​that Huang had “done an amazing job for our country.”
Republican leaders of three House committees have meanwhile called for Huang to deliver closed-door testimony on his interactions with the alleged intelligence asset. Democratic senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons have written to Trump’s commerce secretary Howard Lutnick to demand that all company records relating to Nvidia’s dealings with China be preserved.
Nvidia has started a search for a new permanent CEO and said it had full confidence in Kress, the interim leader.
“Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” said Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia’s board of directors.
“The board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.”
Rhian Lubin contributed to this report from New York

articles.title_orig: Nvidia without Jensen Huang. What lies ahead for Asian chipmakers?
articles.title_zh: Nvidia without Jensen Huang. What lies ahead for Asian chipmakers?
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia's leadership shake-up is unlikely to cause immediate disruption for major Asian semiconductor suppliers, such as Samsung Electronics and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., but Jensen Huang's departure has raised questions about the company's longer-term product strategy and supply chain relationships.
The bigger issue for investors and suppliers is whether Nvidia can maintain the pace of innovation and close ties with key partners that Huang helped drive as the company built its dominance in artificial intelligence chips.
In a Friday research note, Nam Dae-jong and Kim Yeon-mi, analysts at South Korean brokerage Daol Investment & Securities, said Huang's departure was unlikely to affect the semiconductor industry's near-term outlook.
However, they flagged uncertainty over Nvidia's medium- to long-term product roadmap, including how its new leadership would coordinate with partners across the AI ecosystem.
For chipmakers in Asia, one key question is whether Nvidia's relationships with its manufacturing partners could change under new leadership.
Nam and Kim expect Nvidia's foundry relationship with TSMC to remain unchanged, given the companies' established partnership.
They also expect Nvidia's relationship with Samsung's foundry business to continue, citing growing cooperation between the companies, including manufacturing involving Samsung's 4-nanometer process and work on next-generation high-bandwidth memory technology.
The analysts said custom AI chips, or application-specific integrated circuits, or ASICs, are emerging as alternatives to Nvidia's graphic processing units and could accelerate diversification in the AI chip market.
However, they cautioned against interpreting growing competition as a sign of weakening demand for memory semiconductors, particularly high-bandwidth memory, or HBM.
Still, uncertainty remains over Nvidia's longer-term product roadmap, given Huang's central role in shaping the company's business strategy and allocating resources.
SK Hynix, another key supplier to Nvidia, reversed earlier gains to close 3.03% lower on Friday.
In a research note earlier in the day, Shinhan Securities said investors had initially looked past concerns over Nvidia's leadership change and focused instead on the broader outlook for the AI industry.
South Korea's Kospi also reversed earlier gains Friday. In a research note, iM Securities said the impact of Nvidia's leadership change on the broader semiconductor sector appeared limited, pointing to gains in AMD and Broadcom shares in the previous U.S. session and continued investment demand for AI companies.
ASUS Co-CEO S.Y. Hsu told CNBC's " Squawk Box Asia " that Nvidia's leadership change was unlikely to alter its competitive advantages in the near term, though the company would monitor any impact on product quality, service costs and deliveries.
"I think Nvidia's product and the total AI ecosystem, the advantage will not change overnight," Hsu said.
ASUS, which works with Nvidia across graphics cards and AI servers, has yet to interact with interim CEO Colette Kress, Hsu said, adding that the company was seeking a meeting to better understand any potential strategic changes.
Over the longer term, Hsu said Huang had played a key role in helping Nvidia and its partners accelerate innovation, and that he would be watching to see whether the company could maintain that pace without him.

articles.title_orig: Lutnick should have prevented the diversion of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, critics charge
articles.title_zh: Lutnick should have prevented the diversion of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, critics charge
articles.content_orig:
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is under fire from critics asking whether his ties to Chinese companies and friendship with Nvidia's ousted CEO Jensen Huang contributed to the federal agency's lack of oversight over billions in Nvidia AI chip sales, CBS has learned.
Before President Trump nominated Lutnick to lead the Commerce Department, Lutnick was the chairman and CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald, a New York investment bank which held about $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock at the time.
Lutnick developed a warm relationship with Huang, who resigned Thursday as reports of a growing number of affairs caused new uncertainty about the world's dominant AI chipmaker. One of Huang's alleged relationships was with Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen Huang), who is believed by the U.S. to be a Chinese spy. She ran Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based company that became one of Nvidia's biggest customers for AI chips and is suspected of illegally shipping Nvidia's most advanced AI chips to Chinese entities, circumventing a U.S. ban.
As commerce secretary, Lutnick took the helm of an agency responsible for policing exports of sensitive technology to adversaries and global rivals.
One way the Commerce Department keeps this information and technology out of the hands of China and other adversaries is by putting foreign companies and individuals on its Entity List . This restricts their ability to access U.S. technology products, and inclusion on the list means that the department believes there's a risk that the entity is involved in activities that are contrary to U.S. national security or foreign policy interests.
In 2024, under the Biden administration, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security launched an investigation into Nvidia's chip sales to Megaspeed to determine whether they were being redirected to China. But according to The New York Times , the probe was abruptly transferred to the Department of Justice. The Justice Department would not comment about the investigation.
The Commerce Department has not added a company to the Entity List since October 2025.
Last week, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Lutnick over the Commerce Department's failure to place Megaspeed on the Entity List, Axios reported.
Chris McGuire, an expert on China and emerging technologies at the Council on Foreign Relations, said, "The real scandal here is the lack of enforcement of export controls."
He added that the Commerce Department had known for as long as a year that Megaspeed was being run by a woman who is believed by the U.S. to be a Chinese spy, "and they did nothing." The New York Times reported that about a year ago, President Trump was briefed on intelligence that suggested that Alice Huang was a Chinese asset and that she had grown close to Jensen Huang.
"Either Lutnick doesn't know how to do his job or he is protecting Huang," McGuire said.
The Commerce Department did not respond to a request for comment.
On Thursday, after Jensen Huang's resignation became public, Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the ranking Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, called on Lutnick and his deputy, Jeffrey Kessler, to "explain why they have not closed export control loopholes." Kessler is the undersecretary who led the Commerce Department's probe into Megaspeed.
Warren urged the two to "act today to ensure our advanced technology is not fueling China's military." In March, Warren wrote to Lutnick to demand the "immediate pausing" of all export licenses of Nvidia chips destined for China.
Questions about Lutnick's own relationship with Chinese state companies have further complicated the ongoing Nvidia crisis.
A financial services firm Lutnick ran, BGC Group, had a 33% stake in a joint venture with China Credit Trust, a Chinese state-owned company whose largest shareholder is the China People's Insurance Company, another state enterprise.
Another firm he ran, Cantor Fitzgerald, is still overseen by his two eldest sons. That firm helped several Chinese companies go public in the U.S. Cantor Fitzgerald was also a key investor in Satellogic, a satellite company that is under contract with a Chinese data science company, Zhong Ke Guang Qi Space, until 2033.
His close China ties emerged as a topic at his Senate confirmation hearing last year. Senators questioned whether he could be unduly influenced by Chinese officials, and how he would safeguard U.S. technology.
Sen. Maria Cantwell, a Democrat from Washington state, grilled Lutnick on potential conflicts of interest with respect to his investments in Chinese companies, and Cantor Fitzgerald's financial interest in Tether, a cryptocurrency company with a large footprint in China.
Other senators asked about how he would safeguard U.S. technology from the Chinese Communist Party.
"How will you address different threats that we see coming from the CCP within these information and technology markets?" asked GOP Sen. Deb Fischer, of Nebraska.
Lutnick promised to be vigilant against threats from China.
"I take a very jaundiced view of China," he said in response to Fischer. "I think they only care about themselves and seek harm to us, and so we need to protect ourselves."
Before he was sworn in as commerce secretary in February 2025, Lutnick resigned from all of his corporate leadership posts, transferring his business empire to his children.
Since his tenure as commerce secretary began, Lutnick and his family's net worth doubled to $7.3 billion, thanks to his indirect stake in Tether, according to Forbes , which valued his holding in Tether at $5.4 billion. The stake, worth $1.7 billion in early 2025, has more than tripled in value.
"Can we be confident that he is looking out for the public interest?" asked Kathleen Clark, a law professor and expert on government ethics at Washington University in St. Louis. "What's going on with him raises a lot of red flags."
Lutnick's friendship with Jensen Huang may also be problematic, Clark told CBS News.
Huang met Lutnick soon after Lutnick began his term as commerce secretary, Huang told podcaster Joe Rogan last year.
"He started our conversation with, 'Jensen, this is Secretary Lutnick,'" said Huang. "'I just want to let you know that you're a national treasure. Nvidia is a national treasure. And whenever you need access to the president, the administration, you call us.'"
Huang added that every time he called the commerce secretary's office, "if I want to get something off my chest, express some concern, they're always available."
Huang also visited with President Trump. He attended a $1 million-per-person dinner at Mar-a-Lago in April 2025. At that time, Huang tried to convince Mr. Trump to lift restrictions on the company's less advanced H20 chip sales to China, according to The New York Times . Less than three months later, in July 2025, Mr. Trump lifted the restrictions. Nvidia's most advanced chip, the Blackwell, still cannot be sold directly to China.
In July 2025, Lutnick posted a photo to Instagram showing Huang in his trademark black leather jacket standing in the Oval Office next to Mr. Trump, who was seated at his desk. Lutnick is also in the photo along with other visitors.
"Great to meet in the Oval Office with Jensen Huang on the very day Nvidia crossed $4 trillion in market cap," the post said.

articles.title_zh: After meeting Putin, U.S. envoys say Europe to join talks on ending Ukraine war
articles.content_orig:
This blog is now closed. Read below for a roundup of news from two days of talks on Tuesday, November 10 and Wednesday, November 11:
This blog covering the trilateral Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi has now closed. Thank you for reading.
Join us on Thursday for fresh coverage as US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner separatelymeet with the leaders of Russia and Ukraine.
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte offered a characteristically upbeat appraisal of the talks in Abu Dhabi and the prospect of cracks emerging between European NATO members, Ukraine and Donald Trump's administration in the US.
"I was in touch with the NATO team present in Abu Dhabi in the last two days," he told reporters while on a visit to Norway. "What I am getting from those calls is that the US, Ukraine and Europe really being completely aligned and united."
However, he cautioned that "clearly we have to see that the Russian side is willing to play ball."
After more than a decade as prime minister of the Netherlands, Rutte has taken on the unenviable job of trying to keep NATO aligned and united more generally during Donald Trump's second term . He stepped into the role a matter of weeks before the 2024 presidential election in the US.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy landed in Dublin on Wednesday evening, as he and his team head to the ninth European Political Community Summit.
He said both bilateral and multilateral meetings were planned amid his visit to Ireland .
"I will take part in the opening plenary session of the EPC Summit. A meeting on diplomatic efforts with the American negotiating team — Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner — is also planned," he said on social media.
Kushner and Witkoff are first expected to head to Moscow from Abu Dhabi, before moving on to Dublin on Thursday.
The European Political Community is an intergovernmental forum for strategic discussions about the future of Europe. It was set up in 2022, in response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
The group's ninth summit is scheduled to start early on Thursday morning and to continue until roughly the end of the working day. Hosts Ireland are also the current holders of the EU's rotating presidency.
Kyrylo Budanov described the talks in Abu Dhabi as "tough."
"Ukraine's position remains unchanged," Volodymyr Zelenskyy's chief of staff said on Telegram.
"The war must be brought to a halt, and an effective security architecture must be established — on that ensures a lasting peace and makes any recurrence of Russian aggression impossible."
He said returning Ukrainian prisoners was a "specific focus" of the talks, seemingly a reference to the prisoner swap plans, saying "we have achieved a significant result in this regard."
Budanov also thanked US negotiators Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff "for their professionalism, persistence, and efforts in seeking solutions," and thanked the UAE for hosting the talks and supporting the process.
Russia's ambassador to the United States, Alexander Darchiev, has died "suddenly" at the age of 66, the Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday.
Darchiev was quite new in the job, having been appointed in March 2025 shortly after Donald Trump's return to the White House. From 2021 to 2024, he was ambassador to Canada.
The ministry called Darchiev an "outstanding diplomat, an experienced leader and a kind colleague."
It did not provide further details on the death.
Considered a specialist in US relations, Darchiev headed the Russian Foreign Ministry's North America department between 2014 and 2020 before graduating to ambassadorial roles.
When Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, he called the move a "necessary measure."
Russia's chief negotiator Vladimir Medinsky is quoted by state media as saying Moscow saw no possibility of exchanging territory with Ukraine as part of any potential agreement.
State news agency TASS quoted him saying there was "no possibility whatsoever for such exchanges."
TASS and Interfax also both cited Medinsky as saying that Russia had decided to establish a "security zone" along its border with Ukraine following the incursion into Kursk.
"This zone is already quite substantial, it is expanding — and will continue to expand," he said.
The reported comments did not make clear where Medinsky considered the border or the so-called buffer zones to be, quite possibly by design. Russia already claims large chunks of what the international community considers to be Ukraine as parts of its territory following its invasion.
Yuri Ushakov, a foreign policy advisor to Vladimir Putin and part of the Russian negotiating team, on Wednesday described the talks in Abu Dhabi as substantive and very useful.
Moscow's delegation is led by former Culture Minister Vladimir Medinsky, an another aide to Putin.
But Ushakov is also involved, along with deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabko and Mikhail Galuzin, and General Staff officers Igor Kostyukov and Yuri Shigarlovsky on the military side.
German government spokesman Stefan Kornelius has said that following the talks in Abu Dhabi, talks between Chancellor Friedrich Merz and President Vladimir Putin could become more likely.
Asked at a Berlin press conference whether Merz would be ready to speak with Putin, Kornelius said that during the talks in Abu Dhabi negotiators from Europe, the US and Ukraine — but not Russia — had reached an "understanding on the broad outlines."
"This understanding will now be shared with the Russian president. And on that basis, talks may ensue," Kornelius said.
This follows intimations from both sides that the German and Russian leaders might be ready to engage directly.
Russian state news agency Tass cited the Kremlin as saying that Putin would be open to talks with EU leaders including Merz, echoing comments made earlier this year .
Merz, meanwhile, had said last Friday that if Putin were to travel to December's G20 summit in Miami as rumored, he would not rule out a meeting.
Rustem Umerov, currently the head of Ukraine's foreign intelligence service and also its chief negotiator at the talks, also issued a statement following the roughly two hours of trilateral negotiations on Wednesday.
The former defense minister said negotiators discussed "achieving peace and post-war reconstruction," adding that "the first steps towards this must be an end to the war and security guarantees for Ukraine."
Over these two days, the parties were able to state their positions directly, and significant differences remain between them," Umerov said on Telegram.
"There is still a lot of difficult work ahead, but there are opportunities to continue the negotiation process."
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he had received a report on the Abu Dhabi talks from his negotiating team in Abu Dhabi.
He hailed an "important humanitarian arrangement regarding preparations for a new exchange," seemingly a reference to prisoner exchange plans. Zelenskyy also said negotiators discussed "their views on guaranteeing security" for Ukraine, as well as "broader formats for further work involving the Europeans" going forward.
Currently in Copenhagen in Denmark, Zelenskyy said his team would meet US negotiators in Dublin on Thursday, after they head to Moscow. But he also called for more European representation going forward.
"Ukraine's priority is to end the war as soon as possible with a dignified peace," Zelenskyy wrote on social media.
"We believe that Europe must be represented at every stage of real diplomacy. It is essential that the United States have a strong position and exert influence on the source of this war — that is Russia — so that Russia ends the war of its own making."
Ukrainian negotiator David Arakhamia praised "good momentum" after the two-day talks in Abu Dhabi.
"I think that we have a good momentum to bring the solution before the new year comes," Arakhamia said, adding that he hoped another session could be held "as soon as possible."
